intro:
PixelPickle is an easy-to-use photo editor that feels familiar right away: menus, tools and shortcuts are where you expect them. You can retouch photos, paint, work with layers, masks and adjustment layers, draw editable vector shapes and apply dozens of adjustments and effects.

This manual first explains the workspace and the main concepts, then describes every tool, effect and menu command. Shortcuts are written as you type them, for example Ctrl+Z. A complete list is under Help > Keyboard Map.

sections.workspace:
• Menu bar and standard toolbar at the top: files, editing, view, image, effects, layers, selections, windows and help. Commands that need an image are greyed out until you open one.
  • Tool options bar below it: the settings of the current tool, such as size, hardness and opacity. The tool's icon is at the front (hover over it to see its name). Use the Presets button to save and load your own settings. Toggle the bar with F4. Under each number field is a thin bar that shows the value: click or drag on it to change the value quickly (the mouse pointer turns into a double arrow there). You can still type a value or use the arrows.
  • Tools toolbar on the left. A button with a small arrow holds more tools: click the arrow to choose. Without an open image the toolbar is greyed out; with the first image the last used tool is active again.
  • Palettes on the right: Materials (F6), Layers (F8) and History (F3). Show or hide them via View > Palettes or the Palettes button on the standard toolbar, which can also show or hide the Tools toolbar and the Tool Options bar.
  • Status bar at the bottom, which you can hide via View > Toolbars > Status.
  • Right-click the image, a tab or a layer for a context menu with the most useful commands. The menu key or Shift+F10 always opens the image menu, even with tools that use the right mouse button themselves.
  • Icons and buttons follow the accent color of your theme, on light and dark themes alike.
  • PixelPickle is available in 9 languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Chinese and Arabic.
  • When the image is larger than its window, scroll bars appear along the bottom and right side; drag them to move the view.
sections.files:
• File > New (Ctrl+N) creates an empty image. Choose a preset size or type width and height, and pick white, black, transparent, the background color or the foreground color as the background.
  • File > Open (Ctrl+O) opens one or more files. Besides common formats PixelPickle reads .ora, .pspimage, .psd, TGA, PCX, ICO, JPEG 2000 and more. File > Recent Files lists the last ten files you opened or saved.
  • .ora (OpenRaster) is an open standard and the default format for images with layers. It keeps all layers, groups, masks, adjustment layers and editable vector layers.
  • .pspimage files from other photo editors can be opened and, if you like, saved in that format as well. If something cannot be stored exactly, PixelPickle tells you what was adapted.
  • PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP and Targa save a merged image; PixelPickle warns you first, and your layers stay in the open document. For JPEG and WebP you choose the quality.
  • File > Export > GIF Optimizer and JPEG Optimizer give you full control over transparency, colors, quality and subsampling, with a preview.
  • Autosave stores changed images in a recovery folder at an adjustable interval (5 minutes by default). Your own files are never overwritten.
sections.navigation:
• Zoom with the mouse wheel (it zooms around the mouse pointer), with the + and - keys on the numeric keypad, or with the Zoom tool. Ctrl+Alt+N shows the image at 100%.
  • Pan by holding the space bar and dragging, or by dragging with the middle mouse button. Shift+wheel scrolls horizontally and Ctrl+wheel vertically. The Pan tool works too.
  • Window > Fit to Window shows the whole image in its window; Window > Fit to Image (Ctrl+W) makes a floating window the size of the image.
  • Several images can be open at once. By default they are shown as tabs; turn off Window > Tabbed Documents to use floating windows that you can cascade or tile.
  • Switch between images with Ctrl+Tab, by clicking a tab, or via the numbered list at the bottom of the Window menu.
  • Window > New Window opens a second view of the same image, for example one zoomed in and one showing the whole picture.
  • View > Full Screen Edit (Shift+A) uses the whole screen, and View > Grid (Ctrl+Alt+G) shows a grid over the image.
sections.selections:
A selection limits painting, effects and edits to part of the image. The selection tools are the Selection tool (rectangle, ellipse and other shapes), the Freehand selection (freehand, point to point, smart edge and edge seeker) and the Magic Wand (selects by color or brightness).

  • Modes: Replace makes a new selection, Add extends it and Remove cuts a piece out, even when you click inside the selection. Hold Shift to add or Ctrl to remove for a single action.
  • Feather softens the edge by the given number of pixels; Anti-alias smooths jagged edges.
  • Moving: drag inside a selection to move the selected pixels. Drag with the right mouse button to move only the marquee.
  • Arrow keys move the selected pixels 1 pixel, Shift+arrow 10 pixels, and Ctrl+arrow moves only the marquee. With the Move tool and no selection the arrows move the whole layer. Hold an arrow key down and the movement speeds up gradually. The arrow keys also work right after you click a layer in the Layers palette.
  • The Selections menu offers Select All (Ctrl+A), Select None (Ctrl+D), Invert (Ctrl+Shift+I), Expand, Contract, Feather (Ctrl+H), From Mask and Promote Selection to Layer (Ctrl+Shift+P).
  • Ctrl+Shift+M hides the marquee while keeping the selection, so you can judge the result.
sections.layers:
• Raster layers hold pixels; vector layers hold editable lines and shapes; layer groups keep layers together; mask layers control where the layers in their group are visible (white shows, black hides); adjustment layers change everything below them without touching the pixels.
  • Create them via the Layers menu or the buttons in the Layers palette. Drag layers in the palette or use Layers > Arrange to change the order.
  • Set opacity and blend mode per layer, for example Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Soft Light, Difference, Dodge, Burn and Dissolve.
  • Double-click a layer (or use Layers > Properties) for its properties: name, visibility, opacity, blend mode, link set (layers with the same number move together), lock transparency (paint only where the layer already has pixels) and a highlight color for the layer in the palette.
  • On the Blend Ranges tab you decide per channel where the layer is visible, based on the layer itself and on what lies beneath it.
  • For an adjustment layer, Properties reopens its settings so you can change them at any time.
  • A new image starts with a background layer, which cannot be transparent. Promote Background Layer turns it into a normal layer.
sections.materials:
• The Materials palette has two boxes. The top box is the foreground (also the outline of shapes), the bottom box the background (also the fill). The left mouse button paints with the foreground, the right button with the background.
  • Click a box to open Material Properties. There you choose a color (color wheel, swatches, RGB, HSL and HTML code), a gradient (linear, rectangular, sunburst or radial, with angle, repeats, center point and invert) or a pattern (with angle and scale; an open image or your own file works too).
  • Dozens of gradients and patterns are included.
  • Your own gradients: on the Gradient tab, New... opens the Gradient Editor. Click an empty spot below the bar to add a color stop, drag a stop to move it, and give each stop its own color or the foreground or background color, with an opacity. Edit... on a built-in gradient makes an editable copy; Delete removes one of your own gradients. Your gradients are kept for the next time.
  • The small buttons under a box switch quickly between color, gradient and pattern. The transparent button (⊘) turns the material off: no outline or no fill for shapes and text.
  • The swap button (⇅) exchanges foreground and background.
  • Gradients and patterns work with the flood fill, brushes, shapes and text.
sections.vector:
• A vector layer holds objects (lines, curves, shapes) that stay sharp and editable. Create one via Layers > New Vector Layer.
  • With Create on vector turned on in the options bar of the Pen and the shape tools, what you draw becomes an editable object. If the active layer is not a vector layer, PixelPickle makes one for you.
  • To change an object later, choose the Pen in Edit mode and click the line or shape. Drag nodes and handles; Ctrl+drag from a node turns it into a curve. You can also change its colors, line width and line style; Delete removes the object.
  • A line you are drawing stays editable until you press Apply or Enter; Esc discards it.
  • Vector layers stay vector when you move, mirror, rotate or resize them, and when you save as .ora.
  • To paint on a vector layer or apply an effect to it, it must first become a raster layer. PixelPickle asks you to confirm, or you choose Layers > Convert to Raster Layer yourself. After that the objects are ordinary pixels.

The Objects menu works on vector objects: choose them with the Pick tool, then align, distribute, make them the same size, change their order, group them or edit their properties. Convert Text to Curves turns a text layer into vector shapes (as one shape or one per letter), and Fit Text to Path lets a text follow a chosen line or shape.
sections.adjust_effects:
• Most adjustments and effects open a dialog with a before and after preview. You can zoom and pan the preview to look at details.
  • Turn on Preview on image to see the result directly in the image window while you change the settings.
  • Save settings as a preset to recall them quickly later.
  • When a selection is active, the effect only works inside it, and the dialog tells you so.
  • Effects work on the active raster layer. On a text or vector layer PixelPickle first offers to convert it to a raster layer; on an adjustment layer effects do not work.
  • Effects > Effect Browser shows the effects side by side with a small preview of your image, so you can pick one by looking.
  • Adjustment layers (Layers > New Adjustment Layer) apply Brightness/Contrast, Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation/Lightness and more without changing the pixels. You can change or remove them at any time, and paint on them in black and white to limit where they work.
  • Edit > Repeat (Ctrl+Y) applies the last command again.
sections.undo:
Almost everything you do can be undone.

  • Ctrl+Z (or Alt+Backspace) undoes the last step.
  • Ctrl+Alt+Z (or Alt+Shift+Backspace) redoes a step you undid.
  • The History palette (F3) lists every step with its name. Click an earlier step to go back to that point; click a later step to go forward again.
  • When you do something new after going back, the steps after that point are replaced.
  • Undo and redo are also on the standard toolbar and in the context menu of the image.
  • Saving does not clear the history, so you can still undo steps after saving. The history is per image and is lost when you close it.
sections.preferences:
• File > Preferences > General Program Preferences: the language. PixelPickle is available in English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Chinese and Arabic. The new language becomes active after a restart, which PixelPickle can do for you right away.
  • File > Preferences > Autosave Settings: turn autosave on or off and set the interval in minutes. Changed images are kept in a recovery folder (in ~/.local/share/PixelPickle/autosave). Your own files are never overwritten, and the recovery copy disappears when you save or close the image normally.
  • PixelPickle also remembers your tool settings, palette layout, tab mode, last folder and JPEG quality between sessions.
sections.tips:
• Hold the space bar and drag to pan, whatever tool is active.
  • The right mouse button paints with the background color; use it to switch colors without clicking the palette.
  • Save work in progress as .ora so layers, masks and vector objects stay editable; export a PNG or JPEG when you are done.
  • Use an adjustment layer instead of a direct adjustment when you may want to change it later.
  • Ctrl+Shift+M hides the marching ants so you can judge a feathered selection.
  • Ctrl+Y repeats the last command, handy for applying the same effect to several layers.
  • Ctrl+Shift+C copies what you see (all layers merged) instead of only the active layer.
  • Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard as a new image, Ctrl+L as a new layer.
  • For quick portrait retouching use the Makeover tool (blemishes, teeth, eye whites, suntan, slimming); to remove an unwanted object, use the Object Remover.
  • Right-click the empty workspace for New, Open, Close All, the clipboard, the Magnifier and the preferences. With a selection tool, a right-click removes the selection.
  • With brushes that paint a color (paint brush, airbrush, art media, Color Replacer, Change to Target), hold Ctrl and click to pick a color from the image: left for the foreground, right for the background.
  • Help > Keyboard Map lists every shortcut.

menus.e100: Creates a new, empty image (Ctrl+N). You choose the size, from a preset or your own values, and the background: white, black, transparent, or the current background or foreground color.
menus.e101: Opens one or more existing image files (Ctrl+O). If a file is already open, PixelPickle switches to it instead of opening it twice.
menus.e102: Closes the active image (Ctrl+F4). If it has unsaved changes, you are asked whether to save them first.
menus.e103: Saves the active image under its current name (Ctrl+S). An image that was never saved, or is in a format PixelPickle cannot write, asks for a name first.
menus.e104: Saves the image under a new name or in another format (F12). Choose .ora to keep layers; a format without layers saves a merged image after a warning.
menus.e10b: Saves a copy of the image under another name or format (Ctrl+F12) while the open document keeps its own name and stays marked as changed.
menus.814b: Exports a merged JPEG with full control over quality, chroma subsampling and progressive loading. Transparent areas become white.
menus.812d: Exports a GIF with control over transparency (existing transparency, the selection or a chosen color), partly transparent pixels, the number of colors, dithering and interlacing, with a live preview.
menus.8012: Opens the General Program Preferences with three pages. Language: the language of PixelPickle (active after a restart). Transparency and Shading: the size and colors of the checkerboard shown behind transparent areas, and the color and opacity of the shading outside the crop rectangle, plus whether the floating crop toolbar is shown. Fonts: download and install the Microsoft core fonts (Arial, Times New Roman, Verdana and others) from their original source into your own font folder; they can be used right away.
menus.8151: Turns autosave on or off and sets the interval in minutes. Changed images are kept in a recovery folder, never over your own files.
menus.e141: Closes PixelPickle. For every image with unsaved changes you are asked whether to save it.
menus.e12b: Undoes the last step (Ctrl+Z or Alt+Backspace). Use the History palette to go back several steps at once.
menus.e12c: Redoes the step you last undid (Ctrl+Alt+Z or Alt+Shift+Backspace).
menus.e128: Repeats the last command you used (Ctrl+Y), for example to apply the same effect again or to another layer.
menus.e123: Copies the selection (or the whole layer) of the active layer to the clipboard and then clears it (Ctrl+X or Shift+Del).
menus.e122: Copies the selected part of the active layer to the clipboard (Ctrl+C). Without a selection the whole layer is copied.
menus.8105: Copies the selected area as you see it, with all visible layers merged (Ctrl+Shift+C).
menus.80e6: Pastes the clipboard image as a new image in its own window (Ctrl+V or Shift+Ins).
menus.810d: Pastes the clipboard image as a new layer, centered on the active image (Ctrl+L).
menus.801e: Pastes the clipboard image centered on a new layer and selects it (Ctrl+E), so you can drag it into place right away.
menus.801f: Pastes the clipboard image into the current selection, stretched to fit its bounding box (Ctrl+Shift+L). Requires an active selection.
menus.e120: Clears the selection, or the whole layer without a selection (Del). On a background layer the area becomes the background color; on other layers it becomes transparent.
menus.8020: Empties the system clipboard, for example to free memory after copying a large image.
menus.8007: Shows the image at its actual size, one image pixel per screen pixel (Ctrl+Alt+N).
menus.8132: Zooms in one step (+ on the numeric keypad). You can also zoom with the mouse wheel.
menus.8136: Zooms out one step (- on the numeric keypad).
menus.801d: Switches full screen mode on or off (Shift+A), giving you more room for the image.
menus.8021: Shows or hides a grid over the active image (Ctrl+Alt+G), handy for aligning things.
menus.e800: Shows or hides the standard toolbar with buttons for common commands.
menus.e801: Shows or hides the status bar at the bottom of the window.
menus.81f9: Shows or hides the Tools toolbar on the left.
menus.8002: Shows or hides the History palette (F3), which lists every step you can go back to.
menus.81ae: Shows or hides the Layers palette (F8).
menus.8185: Shows or hides the Materials palette (F6) with the foreground and background materials.
menus.81ba: Shows or hides the tool options bar (F4) with the settings of the current tool.
menus.8242: Rotates the whole image 90 degrees clockwise.
menus.8243: Rotates the whole image 90 degrees counterclockwise.
menus.800e: Rotates the whole image by 90, 180 or 270 degrees or by a free angle, clockwise or counterclockwise (Ctrl+R). Corners that become empty get the background color on the background layer.
menus.80d1: Changes the size of the image in pixels or as a percentage, optionally keeping the aspect ratio (Shift+S). Choose smooth (bicubic) resampling for photos or pixel repeat for pixel art.
menus.80d2: Changes the canvas size without scaling the image, so you can add room or cut away edges. Choose where the image is placed; new area on the background layer gets the background color.
menus.807a: Adds a colored border around the image, the same on all sides or set per side. An image with layers is merged first.
menus.80cf: Crops the image to the bounding rectangle of the current selection (Shift+R).
menus.800d: Mirrors the active layer horizontally, left to right (Ctrl+M). With a selection, only the selected pixels are mirrored, in place within the selection, and the selection is mirrored along. Vector and text layers stay editable. Without a selection, the layer is mirrored around the middle of its own content, so a separate figure stays in place.
menus.800c: Flips the active layer vertically, top to bottom (Ctrl+I). With a selection, only the selected pixels are flipped, in place within the selection, and the selection is flipped along. Without a selection, the layer is mirrored around the middle of its own content, so a separate figure stays in place.
menus.80ed: Shows information about the image (Shift+I): file path, dimensions, megapixels, number of layers, file size and memory use.
menus.823f: Counts the number of unique colors in the image as you see it, with all visible layers merged.
menus.807b: Opens the Effect Browser, which shows the effects side by side with a preview of your image. Pick one to open it with its settings.
menus.8140: Adds a new, empty raster layer above the active layer. A dialog lets you set its name, opacity, blend mode and other properties first.
menus.8141: Adds a new vector layer for editable lines and shapes drawn with the Pen and shape tools.
menus.8191: Puts the active layer in a new layer group, so you can move, hide or mask several layers together.
menus.8107: Adds a mask that hides the whole layer (Shift+Y). Paint white on the mask to reveal parts again.
menus.8108: Adds a mask that shows the whole layer. Paint black on the mask to hide parts.
menus.8106: Adds a mask that hides the selected area and shows the rest.
menus.80e9: Adds a mask that shows only the selected area and hides the rest.
menus.80e8: Adds a mask made from the image, based on its brightness (luminance) or on the transparency of the layer, optionally inverted.
menus.8144: Adds a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer that changes everything below it without touching the pixels.
menus.8147: Adds a Channel Mixer adjustment layer, for example for custom black and white conversions.
menus.8145: Adds a Color Balance adjustment layer to shift the colors of shadows, midtones and highlights.
menus.8143: Adds a Curves adjustment layer for precise control over tones and contrast.
menus.8146: Adds a Hue/Saturation/Lightness adjustment layer to change colors, saturation and lightness.
menus.8148: Adds an Invert adjustment layer that turns everything below it into a negative.
menus.8142: Adds a Levels adjustment layer to set the black point, white point and midtones.
menus.814a: Adds a Posterize adjustment layer that reduces the number of brightness levels per channel.
menus.8149: Adds a Threshold adjustment layer that turns everything below it into pure black and white.
menus.80f7: Makes a copy of the active layer directly above it.
menus.8205: Removes the layer group that contains the active layer; its layers stay in place.
menus.80fe: Opens the properties of the active layer: name, visibility, opacity, blend mode, link set, lock transparency, highlight color and the Blend Ranges tab. For an adjustment layer it reopens its settings.
menus.8101: Moves the active layer to the top of the stack.
menus.8104: Moves the active layer one position up.
menus.8102: Moves the active layer one position down.
menus.8103: Moves the active layer to the bottom of the stack.
menus.81d6: Moves the active layer into the layer group directly next to it.
menus.81d7: Moves the active layer out of its group.
menus.81d4: Merges the active layer with the layer below it.
menus.80f8: Merges all layers into one background layer. Transparent areas become white.
menus.8120: Merges all visible layers into one layer; hidden layers are kept as they are.
menus.81d5: Merges all layers of the active group into a single layer.
menus.80ec: Inverts the active mask or adjustment layer (Shift+K), so that hidden areas become visible and vice versa.
menus.821f: Shows the active mask as a colored overlay on the image (Ctrl+Alt+V), so you can see exactly which areas it hides.
menus.80ea: Loads an image file from disk as a new mask; it is scaled to the size of the image.
menus.80eb: Saves the active mask layer to disk as a PNG file, so you can reuse it later.
menus.80fa: Turns a vector or text layer into an ordinary raster layer, so you can paint on it or apply effects. The objects or text are no longer editable afterwards.
menus.815d: Turns the background layer into a normal layer that can be transparent and moved in the stack.
menus.8051: Counts the number of unique colors in the active layer only.
menus.80e2: Removes the selection (Ctrl+D), so that commands work on the whole layer again.
menus.80f5: Makes a selection from the active mask or adjustment layer (Ctrl+Shift+S): white becomes selected, black unselected and grey partly selected.
menus.80dd: Inverts the selection (Ctrl+Shift+I): what was selected becomes unselected and vice versa.
menus.811b: Makes the selection larger by the given number of pixels.
menus.811c: Makes the selection smaller by the given number of pixels.
menus.80e3: Softens the edge of the selection by the given number of pixels (Ctrl+H), for smooth transitions.
menus.811a: Hides or shows the selection marquee (Ctrl+Shift+M). The selection itself stays active.
menus.8109: Copies the selected part of the active layer to a new layer (Ctrl+Shift+P).
menus.e130: Opens a second window on the same image (Shift+W), for example to see it zoomed in and as a whole at the same time.
menus.82ce: Switches between tabbed documents and floating windows.
menus.e132: Arranges the floating image windows in an overlapping cascade.
menus.e133: Arranges the image windows one below the other.
menus.e134: Arranges the image windows side by side.
menus.80d3: Closes all open images, asking to save any unsaved changes.
menus.80d4: Opens a copy of the active image with all its layers as a new, unsaved document (Shift+D).
menus.80d5: Resizes the floating window to fit the image at the current zoom (Ctrl+W). Not available with tabs.
menus.81d0: Zooms the image so it fits entirely in its window.
menus.8028: Shows a list of all keyboard shortcuts for tools and menu commands.
menus.e140: Shows information about PixelPickle, such as the version.
menus.8125: Opens the PixelPickle project page on GitHub in your web browser. The latest version and its release notes are listed there.
menus.80ff: Shows only the active layer and hides all others. If the layer is in a group, the group stays visible; if the active layer is a group, everything in it stays visible. Handy for judging one layer on its own.
menus.8176: Inverts the visibility of every layer: visible layers are hidden and hidden layers are shown. Groups stay visible, so the layers inside them can be seen.
menus.8178: Shows all layers in the link set of the active layer (and the groups they are in). Without a link set, only the active layer is shown.
menus.8179: Hides all layers in the link set of the active layer. Without a link set, only the active layer is hidden.
menus.810f: Saves the current selection in an alpha channel of the image, so you can load it again later. Give it a name, or click an existing channel to overwrite it. Alpha channels are saved in .ora files.
menus.810e: Loads a saved alpha channel as the selection. Choose the channel from the list (a preview shows it); Invert selects the opposite. If there is already a selection, choose whether the channel replaces it, is added to it or is removed from it.
menus.8111: Saves the active mask layer in an alpha channel of the image (white is visible, black is hidden). Give it a name, or click an existing channel to overwrite it.
menus.8110: Adds a new mask layer to the active layer with the content of a saved alpha channel: white parts stay visible, black parts are hidden. Invert does the opposite.
menus.81e4: Deletes one or more alpha channels from the image, or all of them at once. This can be undone.
menus.8216: Shows or hides the Magnifier: a small floating window with an enlarged view of the image under the mouse pointer. Use the mouse wheel in the window to change the magnification (2× to 16×).
menus.8163: Aligns the top edges of the chosen objects with the topmost one. Works on the vector objects chosen with the Pick tool on a vector layer.

menus.8160: Aligns the left edges of the chosen objects with the leftmost one. Works on the vector objects chosen with the Pick tool on a vector layer.

menus.82a8: Converts the active text layer into an editable vector shape (the same as Convert Text to Curves > As Single Shape). Vector objects are already paths.
menus.1770: Cuts the chosen nodes' paths (or all paths) to the Pen's own clipboard. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1771: Copies the chosen nodes' paths (or all paths) to the Pen's own clipboard. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1772: Pastes paths from the Pen's clipboard; the pasted nodes are chosen. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1773: Deletes the chosen nodes; a path with fewer than two nodes left disappears. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1774: Chooses all nodes. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1775: Clears the node selection. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1776: Chooses the nodes that were not chosen, and the other way round. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1777: Joins two chosen end points with a straight segment: two open paths become one path, or the two ends of one path close it. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1778: Merges two chosen end points into one node halfway between them, joining the paths (or closing one path). Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1779: Breaks the path at the chosen nodes: a closed path opens there, an open path splits into two. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177a: Closes the open paths that have chosen nodes (or all paths). Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177b: Reverses the direction of the paths with chosen nodes. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177c: Reverses the direction of all paths and their order. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177d: Duplicates the paths with chosen nodes, shifted 10 pixels to the right and down. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177e: Duplicates the paths with chosen nodes in place. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.177f: Makes the chosen nodes asymmetric: both handles on one line, each with its own length. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.

menus.1782: Makes the chosen nodes smooth: the handles follow the direction of the neighboring nodes, also between a straight segment and a curve. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1783: Turns the segments on both sides of the chosen nodes into straight lines. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1784: Turns the segment before the chosen nodes into a straight line. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1785: Turns the segment after the chosen nodes into a straight line. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1786: Turns the segment before the chosen nodes into a curve with handles. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.1787: Turns the segment after the chosen nodes into a curve with handles. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.

menus.178a: Rotates the chosen nodes around their center by the angle you enter. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.178b: Skews the chosen nodes horizontally by the angle you enter. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.178c: Skews the chosen nodes vertically by the angle you enter. Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.178d: Shrinks the chosen nodes towards their center (by 10% each time). Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.178e: Expands the chosen nodes away from their center (by about 11% each time). Works on the line or shape you are editing with the Pen (also an object picked up in Edit mode); the same command is in the Pen's context menu.
menus.8001: Makes a selection from vector objects: the objects chosen with the Pick tool, or all objects on the active vector layer. Filled shapes and lines are both included.
menus.8114: Extends the selection with all pixels whose color resembles a color in the current selection. Tolerance sets how much colors may differ. With Contiguous on, only areas connected to the current selection are added; with Use all layers on, the merged image is compared.
menus.81eb: Selects pixels by color. Pick a color (the foreground color by default), set the tolerance and softness, and choose whether the result replaces, adds to or removes from the current selection.
menus.8193: Feathers the selection edge only on the inside, only on the outside, or on both sides, over the given number of pixels.
menus.81ee: Removes the feathering of a selection: every pixel above the threshold becomes fully selected, the rest not selected, giving a hard edge again.
menus.81e8: Smooths jagged selection edges with a soft anti-aliased border, either just inside or just outside the edge.
menus.81e7: Recovers the anti-aliasing along the selection edge: the semi-transparent edge pixels of the active layer are included in the selection again, so a cut-out object keeps its smooth edge.
menus.81f6: Removes small loose selected specks and fills small holes in the selection. Set what to remove and the size limit in pixels.
menus.81f5: Smooths the outline of the selection, rounding off small irregularities. Higher amounts give rounder shapes.
menus.81ec: Replaces the selection with a band along its edge: inside, outside or on both sides of the edge, with the width you choose. Handy for strokes and glows.
menus.8283: Removes the part of the selection marquee that fell outside the canvas after moving it, so the selection matches the canvas again.
menus.80de: Loads a selection from an image file: the transparency of the image, or else its brightness (white is selected), becomes the selection. The image is scaled to the canvas.
menus.80df: Saves the current selection as a greyscale PNG image (white is selected), to load it again later or in another image.
menus.81f4: Turns the selection into an editable layer: unselected parts are shown in red. Paint with white to add to the selection, with black to remove, and with grey for partly selected areas, using any brush, fill or tool. Choose the command again to turn it back into a selection. Saving finishes it automatically.
menus.80e4: Floats the selection: the selected pixels move to their own layer above the active layer, so you can move or edit them separately. On the background layer the hole is filled with the background color.
menus.80e5: Defloats the selection: the floating selection is merged into the layer below it again.
menus.012f: Adds a picture frame on a new layer: Simple (in the chosen color), Wood, Gold, Silver, Mat (a passe-partout with a thin frame), Polaroid or Shadow. Set the width and choose whether the frame lies inside the image or around it (the canvas then grows). Adding the frame is one undo step.
menus.8058: Reduces the image to two colors, black and white, based on brightness. Choose the method: Nearest color (flat areas), Error diffusion (fine dither pattern, smoothest result) or Ordered dither (regular pattern).
menus.8059: Reduces the image to 16 colors, using an optimized palette made from the image or a fixed standard palette. Choose the method: Nearest color (flat areas), Error diffusion (fine dither pattern, smoothest result) or Ordered dither (regular pattern). The image stays in full RGB afterwards, so every tool keeps working; all raster layers share the same palette.
menus.805a: Reduces the image to 256 colors, with an optimized or fixed (web) palette. Choose the method: Nearest color (flat areas), Error diffusion (fine dither pattern, smoothest result) or Ordered dither (regular pattern). The image stays in full RGB afterwards, so every tool keeps working; all raster layers share the same palette.
menus.805b: Reduces the color depth to about 32,000 colors (5 bits per channel), with or without ordered dithering.
menus.805c: Reduces the color depth to about 64,000 colors (5 bits for red and blue, 6 for green), with or without ordered dithering.
menus.805d: Reduces the image to a number of colors you choose (2 to 256), with an optimized or fixed palette. Choose the method: Nearest color (flat areas), Error diffusion (fine dither pattern, smoothest result) or Ordered dither (regular pattern). The image stays in full RGB afterwards, so every tool keeps working; all raster layers share the same palette.
menus.80f3: Splits the image into its red, green and blue channels: each becomes a new greyscale image.
menus.8116: Splits the image into hue, saturation and lightness: each becomes a new greyscale image.
menus.8118: Splits the image into cyan, magenta, yellow and black (CMYK): each becomes a new greyscale image.
menus.80f4: Combines three open greyscale images into one color image, as its red, green and blue channels. The images must be the same size.
menus.8117: Combines three open greyscale images as hue, saturation and lightness into one color image.
menus.8123: Combines four open greyscale images as cyan, magenta, yellow and black into one color image.
menus.80f2: Combines two open images pixel by pixel: add, subtract, multiply, difference, lighter, darker, average or the logical AND, OR and XOR. The result is divided by the divisor and the bias is added; Clip keeps values between 0 and 255 (otherwise they wrap around). You can work on all color channels or on one. The result opens as a new image.
menus.80f0: Pastes the clipboard as a new selection on a new layer, like Paste As New Selection, but pixels in the current background color become transparent. Handy for objects copied from a plain background.
menus.8023: Pastes vector objects copied with the Pick tool onto the active vector layer (or a new one). The pasted objects are chosen right away, so you can move them with the Pick tool.
menus.80ef: Shows the whole image on a black full screen, without menus or palettes. Press any key or click to return.
menus.810a: Shows or hides the rulers along the top and left of the image window, in pixels. Drag from a ruler into the image to create a guide.
menus.817c: Shows or hides the guides. Create a guide by dragging from a ruler; drag its handle on the ruler to move it, or back into the ruler to remove it.
menus.817a: When on, points of selections, shapes, the pen, crop and other tools snap to the grid when they come close to it.
menus.817b: When on, points of selections, shapes, the pen, crop and other tools snap to the guides when they come close to them.
menus.8155: Sets the horizontal and vertical grid spacing, the colors of the grid and the guides, and the snap distance (how close, in screen pixels, a point must come to snap).
menus.821d: Shows or hides the Effects toolbar, with buttons for the Effect Browser and popular 3D effects such as Drop Shadow, Inner and Outer Bevel and Buttonize.
menus.821c: Shows or hides the Photo toolbar, with buttons for One Step Photo Fix, Smart Photo Fix, Color Balance, Brightness/Contrast, Brighten, Red Eye Removal, Unsharp Mask and grain removal.
menus.822d: Shows or hides the Brush Variance palette. It adds random variation per dab in size, opacity, rotation and position (scatter) to the paint brush, airbrush and eraser, for a more natural stroke. 0 % means no variation.
menus.8022: Shows or hides the Histogram palette: the distribution of brightness or of the red, green and blue values in the image, with the average and median. It updates while you work.
menus.8159: Shows or hides the Overview palette: a small view of the whole image with a frame around the part visible in the window. Click or drag in it to move the view.
menus.8202: Makes the active image window as large as possible and fits the image in it.
menus.8019: Reloads the last saved version of the image from disk, discarding the changes since then (after confirmation). This can be undone.
menus.80d6: Moves the file of the active image to the trash (after confirmation) and closes the image.
menus.82ec: Prints the image, fitted to the page and centered, with the usual print dialog of your system (printer, paper size, copies).
menus.812e: Shows a print preview of the page, with the image fitted to the page or at its actual size according to its resolution. You can print from the preview.
menus.80e0: Sets up a screen capture: the whole screen, an area you choose or the active window, the delay in seconds and whether PixelPickle hides itself during the capture.
menus.80e1: Takes a screen capture with the settings from Setup; the result opens as a new image. On Wayland desktops the screenshot program of the desktop (such as Spectacle) is used.
menus.8203: Imports one or more images as your own brushes. Dark, opaque parts of the image become the paint of the brush tip. Choose them under Shape in the options bar of the paint brush.
menus.8201: Turns the selection (or the whole image) into your own brush. Dark, opaque parts become paint. The brush appears under Shape in the options bar of the paint brush.
menus.815b: Saves the image as an optimized PNG: 32 bits with transparency, 24 bits without, or an 8-bit palette with a chosen number of colors, with adjustable compression. The expected file size is shown.
menus.8174: Creates an image map for a web page: drag rectangles or circles over the image, give each area a link (URL), an alternative text and a target, and save. PixelPickle writes an HTML page and the image next to it.
menus.822c: Saves the image as your own picture frame for Image > Picture Frame. The frame needs a transparent middle where the photo will show.
menus.815c: Saves the chosen vector objects (or all objects on the vector layer) as your own shape for the Preset Shape tool.
menus.801b: Converts many files in one go to another format (PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP, GIF or OpenRaster), optionally shrunk so the longest side is at most a given size, into a folder of your choice. Existing files are kept unless you choose to overwrite them.
menus.81ad: Renames many files at once: fixed text at the start and end, optionally the old name, and a sequence number with a chosen number of digits. A preview shows the new names before anything is renamed.
menus.8014: Sets the default JPEG quality, the PNG compression and the default format for images with layers (OpenRaster or .pspimage).
menus.8152: Sets the folders for your own brushes, shapes, picture frames and patterns. Patterns in your pattern folder appear in Material Properties and in the Texture and Sculpture effects.
menus.8204: Resets all preferences to their defaults (after a restart). Your own brushes, shapes, frames and gradients in the folders are kept.

d001.about: The Pan tool moves your view of the image without changing it. It is useful when you are zoomed in and the image is larger than the window.
d001.use:
Drag with the left mouse button to shift the view. A right-click without dragging opens the context menu with common commands.

You can pan with any tool: hold the Space bar and drag with the left button, or drag with the middle mouse button.
d001.tips: Because Space and the middle button pan temporarily, you rarely need to switch to this tool while editing.

d002.about: The Zoom tool enlarges or reduces the view of the image. The image itself is not changed.
d002.use: Click with the left mouse button to zoom in one step, centered on the point you click. Click with the right mouse button to zoom out one step.

options.100%: Shows the image at its actual size, where one image pixel is one screen pixel.
options.Passend: Fit: zooms so the whole image fits in the window.

d002.tips: Use 100% to judge sharpness and detail accurately, and Fit to see the whole composition.

d011.about: The Pick tool scales, rotates and moves the contents of the active layer freely. A box with handles appears around the non-transparent pixels of the layer.
d011.use:
• Drag a corner handle to scale in both directions. Hold Shift to keep the proportions.
  • Drag a side handle to stretch or squash in one direction only.
  • Drag the round rotation handle (on the line sticking out of the right side) to rotate around the center. Hold Shift to rotate in steps of 15 degrees.
  • Drag inside the box to move the layer contents.

The status bar shows the scale percentages or the angle while you drag. Each drag is one undo step. Text layers stay editable text when you transform them. A right-click opens the context menu.

On a vector layer the Pick tool chooses objects: click an object, Shift+click to add or remove objects, or drag a frame around them. The handles then move, scale and rotate only the chosen objects. Objects in a group are chosen together. Right-click for the object menu (cut, copy, paste, rename, properties, align, distribute, same size, arrange, group, text on path and Create Raster Selection). The Objects menu has the same commands.
d011.tips: Every new drag starts from the current pixels, so many small scaling steps can soften the image. Try to reach the size you want in one drag.

d012.about: The Move tool shifts the whole active layer, or only the selection marquee, to another position.
d012.use:
Drag with the left mouse button to move the active layer. If the active layer is a group, all layers in it move; linked layers move along. Text and vector layers stay editable.

If there is a selection, drag with the right mouse button to move only the selection marquee, without the pixels. A right-click without dragging opens the context menu.

Arrow keys: without a selection the arrows move the whole layer by 1 pixel. With a selection they move the selected pixels by 1 pixel; hold Shift for 10 pixels, or Ctrl to move only the marquee. Hold an arrow key down and the movement speeds up gradually, up to 8 pixels per step (80 with Shift). Text and vector layers stay editable when moved with the arrow keys. A series of arrow presses counts as one undo step.
d012.tips: To move just the selected pixels with the mouse, use one of the selection tools and drag inside the selection.

d021.about: The Selection tool selects an area with a geometric shape, such as a rectangle, ellipse, triangle, star or arrow. Later edits then only affect the selected area.
d021.use:
Drag with the left mouse button from one corner of the shape to the opposite corner. Press Esc while dragging to cancel. Click without dragging (in Replace mode) to remove the current selection.

Hold Shift when you start dragging to add to the selection, or Ctrl to remove from it.

In Replace mode, dragging inside an existing selection moves the selected pixels; dragging inside it with the right mouse button moves only the marquee. A right-click without dragging opens the context menu.

Arrow keys move the selected pixels by 1 pixel, with Shift by 10 pixels; with Ctrl only the marquee moves.

options.Selectietype:: The shape of the selection. Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle and Ellipse follow the dragged box exactly; Square, Rounded Square and Circle always keep equal width and height. Triangle, Star 1 (five points), Star 2 (eight points) and Right Arrow fill the dragged box with that shape.
options.Modus:: Replace makes a new selection that replaces the current one, Add adds the new area to the existing selection and Remove subtracts it. Holding Shift (add) or Ctrl (remove) while you start overrides this setting for that one action.
options.Doezelen:: Softens the edge of the new selection over this many pixels. At 0 the edge is sharp; higher values give a gradual transition, so edits blend smoothly into the surroundings.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the jagged edge of curved and diagonal selection borders with partially selected pixels.

d021.tips: Use a little feathering when you plan to brighten or recolor a part of a photo, so the edit has no visible edge.

d022.about: The Freehand Selection tool selects irregular areas by drawing their outline, either freely, point by point, or with help that snaps the line to edges in the image.
d022.use:
Freehand: hold the left mouse button and draw around the area; the selection is made when you release the button.

Point to point, Smart Edge, Edge Seeker: click to place points around the area. A line follows the mouse to show the next segment. Finish by double-clicking, right-clicking or pressing Enter. Backspace removes the last point and Esc cancels. The view scrolls automatically when you move near the edge of the window while placing points.

Hold Shift when you start to add to the selection, or Ctrl to remove from it. In Replace mode, dragging inside an existing selection moves the selected pixels (right button: only the marquee). Arrow keys nudge the selection as with the Selection tool.

options.Selectietype:: Freehand follows the mouse exactly while you drag. Point to point connects your clicks with straight lines. Smart Edge snaps each point and segment to the strongest edge nearby. Edge Seeker does the same but searches in a wider area (twice the Range) and more thoroughly, for edges that are less distinct.
options.Modus:: Replace makes a new selection that replaces the current one, Add adds the new area to the existing selection and Remove subtracts it. Holding Shift (add) or Ctrl (remove) while you start overrides this setting for that one action.
options.Doezelen:: Softens the edge of the new selection over this many pixels. At 0 the edge is sharp; higher values give a gradual transition, so edits blend smoothly into the surroundings.
options.Bereik:: For Smart Edge and Edge Seeker: how many pixels away from your clicked line the tool searches for an edge. Higher values find edges further away but may jump to the wrong edge.
options.Vloeiend:: Smooths the outline before the selection is made. At 0 the outline is used as drawn; higher values round off corners and remove small jitters.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the jagged edge of curved and diagonal selection borders with partially selected pixels.
options.Alle lagen gebruiken: For Smart Edge and Edge Seeker: when on, the tool looks at the combined image of all visible layers; when off, it only looks at the active layer.

d022.tips: With Smart Edge, place points close together along soft or low contrast edges, and further apart along clear edges.

d023.about: The Magic Wand selects pixels that resemble the pixel you click, based on color, brightness or opacity. It is ideal for selecting a sky, a plain background or an evenly colored object.
d023.use:
Click on the area you want to select. Hold Shift while clicking to add to the selection, or Ctrl to remove from it.

In Replace mode, clicking and dragging inside an existing selection moves the selected pixels; with the right mouse button only the marquee moves. A right-click without dragging opens the context menu. Arrow keys nudge the selection as with the Selection tool.

options.Modus:: Replace makes a new selection that replaces the current one, Add adds the new area to the existing selection and Remove subtracts it. Holding Shift (add) or Ctrl (remove) while you start overrides this setting for that one action.
options.Overeenkomstmodus:: How pixels are compared with the clicked pixel. None selects everything (limited by Contiguous). RGB Value compares the red, green and blue values. Color looks mainly at the hue and colorfulness and less at brightness. Brightness compares only lightness. Perceptual compares colors the way the eye sees differences. Traditional uses the largest difference in any one color channel. Fully opaque selects all non-transparent pixels. Opacity compares only transparency.
options.Tolerantie:: How different a pixel may be from the clicked pixel and still be selected. 0 selects only exactly matching pixels; higher values select a wider range, and 200 selects everything.
options.Alle lagen gebruiken: When on, the tool looks at the combined image of all visible layers; when off, it only looks at the active layer.
options.Aaneengesloten: When on, only matching pixels connected to the clicked point are selected. When off, all matching pixels in the whole image are selected, also separate areas.
options.Doezelen:: Softens the edge of the new selection over this many pixels. At 0 the edge is sharp; higher values give a gradual transition, so edits blend smoothly into the surroundings.
options.Anti-alias: Gives the selection a smooth edge instead of a hard, stepped one. The list next to it chooses whether the soft edge lies Outside or Inside the matched area.

d023.tips: If the wand selects too little, raise the tolerance or Shift-click additional spots. If it leaks into the background, lower the tolerance.

d030.about: The Dropper picks a color from the image and makes it the foreground or background color.
d030.use: Click with the left mouse button to set the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to set the background color. Keep the button pressed and drag to update the color continuously as you move over the image.

options.Proefgrootte:: The size of the area that is sampled. 1 × 1 takes exactly the clicked pixel; larger sizes take the average color of a square around it, which avoids picking up noise or a single stray pixel.
options.Alle lagen gebruiken: When on, the color is taken from the combined image of all visible layers, as you see it. When off, it is taken from the active layer only.

d030.tips: The picked color is always fully opaque. Use a sample size of 3 × 3 or 5 × 5 on photos for a more representative color.

d040.about: The Crop tool cuts the image down to a rectangle you choose, removing everything outside it. All layers are cropped.
d040.use:
Drag a rectangle over the image. The area outside it is darkened. Drag the handles on the corners and sides to resize it, and drag inside it to move it.

A small floating bar appears near the rectangle with a check mark to apply, a button to swap the rectangle between landscape and portrait, and a list of fixed proportions (Free form, 1 × 1, 4 × 3, 3 × 2, 16 × 9, 5 × 4, 7 × 5, A4).

Apply the crop by double-clicking inside the rectangle, pressing Enter, clicking the check mark or choosing Apply crop in the right-click menu. Press Esc (or choose Clear crop rectangle) to remove the rectangle without cropping. The status bar shows the size while you drag.

options.Breedte:: The width of the crop rectangle in pixels. Type a value to set it exactly.
options.Hoogte:: The height of the crop rectangle in pixels.
options.Links:: The position of the left edge of the rectangle, in pixels from the left of the image.
options.Boven:: The position of the top edge, in pixels from the top of the image.
options.Rechts:: The position of the right edge, in pixels from the left of the image.
options.Onder:: The position of the bottom edge, in pixels from the top of the image.
options.Verhouding behouden: Locks the current width to height ratio of the rectangle, so resizing it (with the mouse or by typing a width or height) keeps the same proportions.
options.⬚: Snaps the crop rectangle to the whole current image.
options.▣: Snaps the crop rectangle tightly around the non-transparent parts of the active layer.
options.◼: Snaps the crop rectangle tightly around the non-transparent parts of all layers combined.

d040.tips: Choose a fixed proportion such as 3 × 2 or 4 × 3 in the floating bar when you crop for prints in a standard size.

d051.about: The Straighten tool rotates the whole image so that a crooked line, such as a horizon or a wall, becomes perfectly horizontal or vertical.
d051.use:
Drag a line along an edge that should be straight. You can then drag either end point to adjust it, or drag a new line elsewhere. Apply by double-clicking, pressing Enter, clicking Apply or choosing Apply straighten in the right-click menu. Esc removes the line.

All layers are rotated. Corners that become empty on the background layer are filled with the background color.

options.Modus:: Automatic makes the line horizontal if it runs mostly sideways and vertical if it runs mostly up and down. Make horizontal and Make vertical force one of the two.
options.Afbeelding bijsnijden: When on, the rotated image is cropped to the largest rectangle without empty corners. When off, the canvas grows to hold the whole rotated image.
options.Toepassen: Rotates the image according to the drawn line.

d051.tips: Draw the line as long as possible along the reference edge; a longer line gives a more accurate angle.

d052.about: The Perspective Correction tool straightens objects photographed at an angle, such as converging walls of a building or a document shot from the side.
d052.use:
A frame with four corner handles appears on the image. Drag each corner onto the corresponding corner of the object that should be rectangular. Drag inside the frame to move it as a whole.

Apply by double-clicking inside the frame, pressing Enter, clicking Apply or choosing Apply perspective correction in the right-click menu. Esc, Reset or Reset frame in the right-click menu puts the frame back in its starting position.

options.Rasterlijnen:: The number of grid lines drawn inside the frame in each direction. The grid helps you line the frame up with lines in the image; 0 shows no grid.
