options.Tolerantie:: How much a pixel may differ from the color to replace and still be replaced. At 0 only exactly matching pixels change; higher values also replace similar shades.

d0ac.tips: The replacement color is solid, so subtle shading in the replaced area is lost. For recoloring with shading kept, use Change to Target or the Color Changer instead.

d0b0.about: The Eraser removes pixels from the active layer by making them transparent, so the layers below (or the transparency checkerboard) show through.
d0b0.use: Drag over the image with the left or right mouse button to erase. Hold Shift and click to erase a straight line from the end of the previous stroke to the click point. Erasing is limited to the active selection when one exists.

options.Vorm:: The shape of the brush tip. Round gives a circular tip; Square gives a square tip with hard edges (Hardness has no effect on a square tip).
options.Grootte:: The diameter of the brush in pixels. Larger values affect a wider area with each dab.
options.Hardheid:: How sharp the edge of the brush is. At 100 the effect is equally strong up to the edge; lower values fade the effect out softly towards the edge.
options.Stap:: The distance between dabs along a stroke, as a percentage of the brush size. Low values give a smooth, continuous stroke; high values leave separate dabs with gaps between them.
options.Dichtheid:: The percentage of pixels inside the brush that is affected by each dab. At 100 the whole tip works; lower values give a speckled, spray-like result.
options.Dikte:: Squashes the brush tip vertically. At 100 the tip is as tall as it is wide; lower values make it flatter, like a calligraphy nib.
options.Rotatie:: Rotates the brush tip in degrees. This only makes a visible difference when Thickness is below 100 or the shape is Square.
options.Dekking:: How much is erased. At 100 the pixels become fully transparent; lower values only make them partly transparent, and going over them again in a new stroke erases more.

d0b0.tips: A low Hardness gives soft edges, which is useful for blending one layer into another. For non-destructive work, consider a mask instead of erasing.

d0c0.about: The Background Eraser erases only the pixels that look like the color under the center of the brush. It is made for removing a background around an object while leaving the edges of the object intact.
d0c0.use: Drag along the edge of the object with the left or right mouse button, keeping the center of the brush (the crosshair point) on the background you want to remove. Pixels similar to that color become transparent; different colors under the brush are kept. Hold Shift and click to erase along a straight line from the end of the previous stroke.

options.Vorm:: The shape of the brush tip. Round gives a circular tip; Square gives a square tip with hard edges (Hardness has no effect on a square tip).
options.Grootte:: The diameter of the brush in pixels. Larger values affect a wider area with each dab.
options.Hardheid:: How sharp the edge of the brush is. At 100 the effect is equally strong up to the edge; lower values fade the effect out softly towards the edge.
options.Stap:: The distance between dabs along a stroke, as a percentage of the brush size. Low values give a smooth, continuous stroke; high values leave separate dabs with gaps between them.
options.Dichtheid:: The percentage of pixels inside the brush that is affected by each dab. At 100 the whole tip works; lower values give a speckled, spray-like result.
options.Dikte:: Squashes the brush tip vertically. At 100 the tip is as tall as it is wide; lower values make it flatter, like a calligraphy nib.
options.Rotatie:: Rotates the brush tip in degrees. This only makes a visible difference when Thickness is below 100 or the shape is Square.
options.Dekking:: The strength of the effect. At 100 it works at full strength; lower values blend the result with the original pixels.
options.Tolerantie:: How much a pixel may differ from the sampled color and still be erased. Low values erase only very similar colors; higher values also erase colors that are further away. The transition is soft, so nearly matching pixels become partly transparent.
options.Bemonstering:: How the color to erase is chosen. Continuous samples the color under the brush center at every dab, so it follows a background that changes in color. One time samples the color only at the start of the stroke and erases that color for the whole stroke.

d0c0.tips: Use One time sampling when the background is a single color and the object has similar colors near the edge, so the brush does not start erasing the object when you stray onto it.

d0d1.about: The Flood Fill tool fills an area of similar pixels with a color, gradient or pattern. The area is found starting from the point you click and spreads out to connected pixels that match.
d0d1.use: Click with the left mouse button to fill with the foreground color or material, or with the right mouse button to fill with the background color or material. When a gradient or pattern is set as material, it is spread over the filled area. When a selection exists, only the part of the area inside the selection is filled; clicking outside the selection does nothing.

options.Overeenkomstmodus:: How pixels are compared with the clicked pixel to decide whether they belong to the area. None fills everything connected; RGB Value compares the red, green and blue values; Color compares mainly the color and less the brightness; Brightness compares only brightness; Perceptual compares colors the way the eye sees differences; Traditional uses the largest difference in any single channel; Fully opaque fills all connected pixels that are not transparent; Opacity compares only the transparency.
options.Tolerantie:: How much a pixel may differ from the clicked pixel and still be filled. At 0 only identical pixels are filled; higher values fill a wider range of similar pixels. At 200 everything connected is filled.
options.Alle lagen gebruiken: When on, the area is determined from the visible image with all layers combined, but the fill is still painted on the active layer. When off, only the active layer is used to find the area.
options.Mengmodus:: How the fill color is combined with the existing pixels. Normal simply covers them; the other modes (such as Multiply, Screen, Overlay or Color) mix the fill with what is already there, just like layer blend modes. Behind paints only where the layer is transparent, so existing pixels stay in front.
options.Dekking:: The opacity of the fill. At 100 the area is completely covered; lower values let the original pixels show through.

d0d1.tips: To fill an empty transparent layer completely, set Match mode to None, or fill a transparent area with Opacity mode. Raise the tolerance a little when a fill leaves a thin fringe of unfilled pixels along antialiased edges.

d0d2.about: The Color Changer recolors a color everywhere in the layer with one click, while keeping its light and shadow. All similar colors change along, also in separate areas, and darker and lighter parts stay darker and lighter relative to each other.
d0d2.use: Click with the left mouse button on a color to change it into the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to change it into the background color. Pixels are compared mainly by their hue, so the shadow side of the same object changes along with the lit side. The pixels get the hue and saturation of the new color, and their lightness is shifted by the difference between the clicked pixel and the new color. Only the active layer is used, and a selection limits the change.

options.Tolerantie:: How much a color may differ from the clicked color and still be changed. Low values change only very similar colors; higher values include a wider range of related colors.
options.Randzachtheid:: How gradually the change fades out for colors just outside the tolerance. At 0 a color is either changed or not; higher values give smoother transitions.
options.Aaneengesloten: Off by default: all matching colors on the whole layer change, also in separate areas. When on, only pixels connected to the clicked point are changed.
options.Dekking:: The strength of the change. At 100 the new color is applied fully; lower values blend it with the original color.

d0d2.tips: Pick a target color with roughly the same lightness as the area you click for the most natural result, for example when recoloring a car or a wall.

d0f0.about: The Text tool adds text to your image. Every text is placed on its own text layer and stays editable: you can change the words, font, size and colors later without loss of quality.
d0f0.use:
Click with the left mouse button on the image where the text should start. A new text layer is created and the Enter text window opens. Type your text; press Enter in the text box for a new line. The text appears on the image right away and you can still change the options in the options bar while the window is open. Click Apply to finish or Cancel to throw the text away. If you leave the text empty, the new layer is removed again.

To edit existing text, click on it with the Text tool. The layer becomes active, the options bar takes over the settings of that text and the window opens with the current text. Cancel restores the text as it was.

Formatting single words: the options bar sets the formatting of the whole text. To give some words their own formatting, select them in the Enter text window and use the small toolbar above the text box: bold, italic, underline, color, font and size. The eraser button clears the formatting of the selection, so it follows the options bar again. Edited later, the text keeps this formatting.

The fill of the letters uses the background material and the outline uses the foreground material. Both can also be a gradient or a pattern; a gradient runs across the whole text. Words with their own color keep that color. Set the background to transparent for outlined letters only. Tick Remember text in the window to start with the same text the next time you create a new text.

options.Lettertype:: The font family of the text. All fonts installed on your system are listed.
options.Grootte:: The size of the letters, in the unit chosen under Units.
options.Eenheden:: The unit for the size. Points depend on the resolution of the image, so the same point size looks larger in a high resolution image; Pixels give an exact height in pixels regardless of resolution.
options.Vet: Shows the text in a bold weight.
options.Onderstreept: Draws a line under the text.
options.Uitlijning:: How the lines are placed relative to the point you clicked. Left starts each line at that point, Center centers each line on it, and Right ends each line at it. This matters most for text with several lines.
options.Lijnbreedte:: The width of the outline around the letters, drawn in the foreground color. At 0 the letters have no outline.
options.Regelafstand:: Extra space between lines in pixels, added to the normal line spacing of the font. Negative values bring the lines closer together; positive values spread them apart.
options.Spatiëring:: Extra space between letters. Positive values spread the letters apart; negative values squeeze them together.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the letters. Turn it off for sharp, pixel-exact text, for example very small text for icons or pixel art.

d0f0.tips: Because each text lives on its own layer, you can move it, change its layer opacity or add effects to it without touching the rest of the image. Click the text again with the Text tool at any time to fix a typo.

d101.about: The Preset Shape tool draws ready-made shapes such as arrows, a star, a heart, speech balloons and a lightning bolt with a single drag.
d101.use: Drag with the left mouse button on the image from one corner of the shape to the opposite corner. You see the shape while you drag; when you release the button it is finished. Hold Shift while dragging to make the width and height equal. The outline uses the foreground color or material and the fill uses the background color or material. Set the foreground to transparent for a shape without an outline, or the background to transparent for an outline only.

options.Vorm:: The shape to draw: Right, Left, Up or Down Arrow, a five-pointed Star, Heart, Speech Balloon, Thought Cloud, Lightning Bolt, Cross, Hexagon or Starburst (a sixteen-pointed star). The shape is stretched to fill the rectangle you drag.
options.Lijnbreedte:: The width of the outline in pixels, drawn in the foreground color or material. At 0 the shape gets no outline, only a fill.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the shape so they do not look jagged. Turn it off for crisp, pixel-exact edges.
options.Op vector maken: When on, the shape is placed as an editable object on a new vector layer instead of being painted as pixels. If the active layer already is a vector layer, the shape always becomes an object on it.

d101.tips: Turn on Create on vector if you want to change the shape later: you can then pick it up with the Pen tool in Edit mode and move its nodes. A shape painted as pixels can only be changed with the paint tools. A shape is limited to the active selection when one exists.

d102.about: The Rectangle tool draws rectangles and squares, optionally with rounded corners.
d102.use: Drag with the left mouse button on the image from one corner of the shape to the opposite corner. You see the shape while you drag; when you release the button it is finished. Hold Shift while dragging to draw a perfect square. The outline uses the foreground color or material and the fill uses the background color or material. Set the foreground to transparent for a shape without an outline, or the background to transparent for an outline only.

options.Hoekradius:: The radius of the rounded corners in pixels. At 0 the corners are sharp; higher values give rounder corners.
options.Lijnbreedte:: The width of the outline in pixels, drawn in the foreground color or material. At 0 the shape gets no outline, only a fill.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the shape so they do not look jagged. Turn it off for crisp, pixel-exact edges.
options.Op vector maken: When on, the shape is placed as an editable object on a new vector layer instead of being painted as pixels. If the active layer already is a vector layer, the shape always becomes an object on it.

d102.tips: Turn on Create on vector if you want to change the shape later: you can then pick it up with the Pen tool in Edit mode and move its nodes. A shape painted as pixels can only be changed with the paint tools. A shape is limited to the active selection when one exists.

d103.about: The Ellipse tool draws ovals and circles.
d103.use: Drag with the left mouse button on the image from one corner of the shape to the opposite corner. You see the shape while you drag; when you release the button it is finished. Hold Shift while dragging to draw a perfect circle. The outline uses the foreground color or material and the fill uses the background color or material. Set the foreground to transparent for a shape without an outline, or the background to transparent for an outline only.

options.Lijnbreedte:: The width of the outline in pixels, drawn in the foreground color or material. At 0 the shape gets no outline, only a fill.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the shape so they do not look jagged. Turn it off for crisp, pixel-exact edges.
options.Op vector maken: When on, the shape is placed as an editable object on a new vector layer instead of being painted as pixels. If the active layer already is a vector layer, the shape always becomes an object on it.

d103.tips: Turn on Create on vector if you want to change the shape later: you can then pick it up with the Pen tool in Edit mode and move its nodes. A shape painted as pixels can only be changed with the paint tools. A shape is limited to the active selection when one exists.

d104.about: The Symmetric Shape tool draws regular polygons, such as triangles, pentagons and hexagons, and stars with any number of points.
d104.use: Press the left mouse button where the center of the shape should be and drag outwards. The distance you drag sets the size and the direction sets the rotation, so the first corner points towards the mouse. Release the button to finish. The outline uses the foreground color or material and the fill uses the background color or material.

options.Aantal zijden:: The number of corners of the polygon, or the number of points when Star is on.
options.Ster: When on, the tool draws a star instead of a polygon, with inner corners between the points.
options.Straal binnen:: Only used for stars: the distance of the inner corners from the center, as a percentage of the outer radius. Low values give thin, sharp points; high values give a fuller, blunter star.
options.Lijnbreedte:: The width of the outline in pixels, drawn in the foreground color or material. At 0 the shape gets no outline, only a fill.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the shape so they do not look jagged. Turn it off for crisp, pixel-exact edges.
options.Op vector maken: When on, the shape is placed as an editable object on a new vector layer instead of being painted as pixels. If the active layer already is a vector layer, the shape always becomes an object on it.

d104.tips: Turn on Create on vector if you want to change the shape later: you can then pick it up with the Pen tool in Edit mode and move its nodes. A shape painted as pixels can only be changed with the paint tools. A shape is limited to the active selection when one exists.

d110.about: The Pen tool draws straight lines, polylines, smooth Bezier curves and freehand lines. The line stays editable, so you can move its nodes and handles, until you apply it to the layer or turn it into an object on a vector layer.
d110.use:
Choose a mode in the options bar and draw with the left mouse button:

  • Lines and polylines: drag from the start point to the end point for a straight line, or click a start point and then click again for the end point. Hold Shift to snap the angle to steps of 45 degrees. With Connect segments on, each new line continues from the end of the previous one.
  • Point to point (Bezier curves): click to place a corner point, or press and drag to place a smooth point and pull out its curve handles. Click on the first point (shown in green) to close the path. Double-click to end the current line so the next click starts a new one.
  • Freehand: hold the mouse button and draw. When you release, the line is simplified according to Tracking.
  • Edit: drag nodes to move them (their handles move along) and drag handles to change the curve; the opposite handle mirrors so the node stays smooth. Hold Ctrl and drag from a corner node to pull out handles and turn it into a curve. Click a node to select it (shown in red) and press Delete to remove it.

Right-click for a context menu with Apply path and, when a node is selected, Smooth node, Corner node and Close path or Open path.

Press Enter or click Apply to put the line on the layer; press Esc to throw it away. Switching to another tool also applies the line. The line uses the foreground color or material; closed paths are filled with the background color or material.

On a vector layer, Edit mode also lets you click an existing object to pick it up: it becomes editable again and its colors and line settings are loaded into the options bar. Esc puts it back unchanged, Delete (with no node selected) removes the object, and Apply saves your changes.

Choosing nodes: in Edit mode, click a node to choose it, Shift+click to add or remove nodes, or drag a frame around several nodes. Dragging a chosen node moves all chosen nodes. How the handles move depends on the node type (symmetric, asymmetric, cusp or smooth).

Context menu: right-click while a line is being edited for the Edit, Node Type and Transform Selected Nodes menus (join, merge, break, close, reverse, duplicate, node types, flip, mirror, rotate, skew, shrink and expand). The same commands are in the Objects menu.

options.✓ Toepassen: Puts the current line on the layer: as pixels on a normal layer, or as an editable object on a vector layer. Same as pressing Enter.
options.Modus:: The way of drawing. Edit moves existing nodes and handles and picks up objects on a vector layer; Lines and polylines draws straight segments; Point to point (Bezier curves) places corner and smooth curve points; Freehand follows the mouse.
options.Tracking:: Only for Freehand: how much the drawn line is simplified. Low values follow the mouse closely with many nodes; higher values give a smoother line with fewer nodes.
options.Segmenten verbinden: When on, each new segment or freehand stroke continues from the end of the current line, so you build one connected polyline. When off, every drag starts a separate line.
options.Knooppunten tonen: Shows the nodes and curve handles of the line on the canvas. Turn it off to see the line without the editing markers.
options.Op vector maken: When on and the active layer is a normal layer, Apply places the line on a new vector layer as an editable object instead of painting it as pixels. On a vector layer the line always becomes an object.
options.Lijnstijl:: The pattern of the line: Solid, Dashes, Dots, Dash-dot or Dash-dot-dot.
options.Breedte:: The width of the line in pixels. At 0 there is no outline; a closed path is then only filled.
options.Anti-alias: Smooths the edges of the line. Turn it off for hard, pixel-exact lines.
options.Verbinding:: How the line looks at corners. Miter gives sharp pointed corners, Round gives rounded corners (and round line ends), and Bevel cuts the corners off flat.
options.Verstek:: Only for Miter joins: the limit for how far a sharp corner may stick out, relative to the line width. If a very sharp corner exceeds it, the corner is cut off like a bevel. Higher values allow longer points.

d110.tips: Turn on Create on vector when you expect to change the line later. You can then return at any time with the Pen in Edit mode, click the object and adjust it. A line applied as pixels on a normal layer is limited to the active selection.

d121.about: The Warp Brush pushes, bulges, pinches and twirls the pixels of the image as if it were made of soft rubber. It is useful for retouching shapes and for playful distortions.
d121.use: Choose a mode and drag over the image with the left or right mouse button. Hold Shift and click to warp along a straight line from the end of the previous stroke. As long as the layer is not changed by another tool, all warping is kept as one distortion of the original pixels, so you can keep working and use Iron out to bring distorted areas back towards their original state.

options.Modus:: What the brush does. Push drags the pixels along in the direction you move; Expand bulges them outwards from the center of the brush; Contract pinches them towards the center; Twirl right and Twirl left rotate them clockwise or counterclockwise; Noise moves pixels randomly for a rippled look; Iron out gradually restores warped pixels to their original position.
options.Grootte:: The diameter of the brush in pixels. A larger brush distorts a wider area at once.
options.Hardheid:: How large the fully affected center of the brush is. The effect always fades out smoothly towards the edge of the brush, so no seams or tears appear; at 100 the center is largest, lower values make the transition wider and softer.
options.Sterkte:: How strongly each dab distorts the pixels. Low values give fine, controlled changes; high values give a strong effect quickly.
options.Randmodus:: What appears where pixels are pulled in from outside the image. Repeat stretches the edge pixels; Transparent leaves transparent pixels; Wrap takes pixels from the opposite side of the image; Mirror uses a mirrored copy of the image.

d121.tips: Use Expand and Contract with a soft, large brush and low strength for subtle retouching, for example making eyes slightly bigger. The brush only works while it moves, so drag in small circles over the spot you want to change.

d122.about: Mesh Warp places a grid over the image. When you drag the nodes of the grid, the image bends along with it, which lets you reshape parts of a picture smoothly.
d122.use:
Drag a node (a small white square) with the left mouse button; the image is reshaped when you release. Hold Shift while dragging to move the whole row of nodes, or Ctrl to move the whole column. The nodes on the outer edge can be moved too.

Click Reset or press Esc to put the grid back and undo all mesh changes since the last apply. Click Apply or press Enter to accept the result: the current image becomes the new starting point with a fresh, straight grid. The context menu (right mouse button) also offers Reset grid and Apply grid.

options.Kolommen:: The number of grid columns between the image edges. More columns give finer control over smaller areas.
options.Rijen:: The number of grid rows between the image edges. More rows give finer control over smaller areas.
options.Herstellen: Puts all nodes back in their original straight positions and restores the image as it was at the start (or since the last Apply). Same as pressing Esc.
options.Toepassen: Accepts the current distortion. The result becomes the new starting point and a fresh, straight grid is shown so you can continue warping. Same as pressing Enter.

d122.tips: Start with a few rows and columns for large, smooth changes. Changing the number of rows or columns resets the grid, so choose the grid size before you start dragging.

d131.about: The Oil Brush paints thick oil paint with visible bristle marks. The paint mixes with the colors already on the layer and slowly runs out during a stroke, just like a real loaded brush.
d131.use: Drag with the left mouse button to paint with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to paint with the background color. The bristle marks follow the direction of your stroke. As you paint over existing colors, the brush picks some of them up and carries them along, and as the paint on the brush runs out the stroke becomes thinner and takes on more of the picked-up color. Each new stroke starts with a fully loaded brush. Hold Shift and click to paint a straight line from the end of the previous stroke.

options.Grootte:: The size of this medium in pixels. Each art medium remembers its own size, separate from the other brushes.
options.Dekking:: The maximum opacity of the stroke. Lower values give a more transparent, lighter stroke.
options.Lading:: How much paint the brush holds. High values let you paint long strokes with fresh color; at 100 the paint never runs out. Low values make the paint run out quickly, so the stroke soon blends into the colors underneath.
options.Viscositeit:: How strongly the brush picks up and mixes in the colors already on the layer. At 0 the color stays pure; higher values smear more of the existing colors into the stroke.

d131.tips: Paint on a normal raster layer. For a painterly look, use short strokes in different directions and a medium Viscosity so neighboring colors blend.

d132.about: Chalk draws a dry, grainy stroke that sticks to the raised parts of the paper texture, like chalk on a rough board.
d132.use: Drag with the left mouse button to draw with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to draw with the background color. Hold Shift and click to draw a straight line from the end of the previous stroke to the click point. Within one stroke the paint does not build up: going over the same spot again in the same stroke keeps the strongest coverage, so the grain stays visible. Start a new stroke over the same area to make it fuller.

options.Grootte:: The size of this medium in pixels. Each art medium remembers its own size, separate from the other brushes.
options.Dekking:: The maximum opacity of the stroke. Lower values give a more transparent, lighter stroke.
options.Korrel:: The strength of the paper texture. At 0 the stroke is smooth; higher values let more of the paper grain show through, so pigment only sticks to the raised parts of the paper.

d132.tips: Draw over the same area with several separate strokes to fill in more of the grain. Light chalk on a dark layer gives a blackboard effect.

d133.about: Pastel draws a soft, well covering stroke with a fine paper grain, like soft pastel crayons.
d133.use: Drag with the left mouse button to draw with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to draw with the background color. Hold Shift and click to draw a straight line from the end of the previous stroke to the click point. Within one stroke the paint does not build up: going over the same spot again in the same stroke keeps the strongest coverage, so the grain stays visible. Start a new stroke over the same area to make it fuller.

options.Grootte:: The size of this medium in pixels. Each art medium remembers its own size, separate from the other brushes.
options.Dekking:: The maximum opacity of the stroke. Lower values give a more transparent, lighter stroke.
options.Korrel:: The strength of the paper texture. At 0 the stroke is smooth; higher values let more of the paper grain show through, so pigment only sticks to the raised parts of the paper.

d133.tips: Pastel covers more than Chalk. Lower the Grain for smooth color areas, or raise it for a textured paper look.

d134.about: Colored Chalk draws a waxy stroke with a coarse grain and irregular edges, like a wax crayon. The color varies slightly from dab to dab.
d134.use: Drag with the left mouse button to draw with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to draw with the background color. Hold Shift and click to draw a straight line from the end of the previous stroke to the click point. Within one stroke the paint does not build up: going over the same spot again in the same stroke keeps the strongest coverage, so the grain stays visible. Start a new stroke over the same area to make it fuller.

options.Dekking:: The maximum opacity of the stroke. Lower values give a more transparent, lighter stroke.
options.Korrel:: The strength of the paper texture. At 0 the stroke is smooth; higher values let more of the paper grain show through, so pigment only sticks to the raised parts of the paper.

d134.tips: Great for childlike drawings and rough coloring. A high Grain leaves many small white gaps in the stroke.

d135.about: Colored Pencil draws fine lines with paper grain, suitable for sketching and hatching. Its default size is small, like a sharpened pencil tip.
d135.use: Drag with the left mouse button to draw with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button to draw with the background color. Hold Shift and click to draw a straight line from the end of the previous stroke to the click point. Within one stroke the paint does not build up: going over the same spot again in the same stroke keeps the strongest coverage, so the grain stays visible. Start a new stroke over the same area to make it fuller.

options.Grootte:: The size of this medium in pixels. Each art medium remembers its own size, separate from the other brushes.
options.Dekking:: The maximum opacity of the stroke. Lower values give a more transparent, lighter stroke.
options.Korrel:: The strength of the paper texture. At 0 the stroke is smooth; higher values let more of the paper grain show through, so pigment only sticks to the raised parts of the paper.

d135.tips: Build up shading with several layers of parallel hatching strokes. Lower the Opacity for light sketch lines.

d070.about: The Makeover tool does quick portrait retouching. It has five modes: removing blemishes, whitening teeth, brightening the whites of the eyes, giving skin a suntan, and making a person look slimmer.
d070.use:
Choose a mode in the options bar.

  • Remove Blotches: click on a spot or pimple, or drag over several. The circle is filled from the skin around it, so the spot disappears and the skin tones flow on naturally. Make the size a bit larger than the spot.
  • Toothbrush: paint over the teeth. Light, yellowish pixels become whiter; lips and gums stay as they are, because red tones are left alone.
  • Eye Drop: paint over the whites of the eyes. Red veins fade and the white becomes a little brighter; the darker iris is hardly affected.
  • Suntan: paint over the skin to give it a warm, tanned tint. Light and shadow are kept.
  • Thinify: click in the middle of a person. The image is squeezed horizontally towards that point, so the person looks slimmer. The edges of the image stay in place. Click again for a stronger effect.

Like the other retouch brushes, the brush modes work once per stroke: going back and forth over the same spot does not build up the effect.

options.Modus:: Remove Blotches, Toothbrush, Eye Drop, Suntan or Thinify. See above for what each mode does.
options.Grootte:: Diameter of the brush in pixels. For Remove Blotches, choose it slightly larger than the spot. Not used by Thinify.
options.Sterkte:: How strong the effect is. For Thinify it sets how much narrower the image gets around the clicked point (up to 12%).

d070.tips: Zoom in for precise work on teeth and eyes, and use a selection if you want to be sure nothing outside an area changes.

d083.about: The Object Remover removes an unwanted object, such as a can on a table, a sign or a passer-by, and fills its place with background from elsewhere in the image. Colors and brightness are matched to the surroundings, so no visible seam appears.
d083.use: In Select mode, drag a line around the object. When you release the mouse button the outline closes and the tool switches to Source mode: a box the size of the object appears next to it. Drag the box over a piece of background that would fit in the object's place; drag a corner to make it bigger or smaller. Then click Apply or press Enter. Esc discards the outline.

options.Modus:: Select: draw the outline around the object. Source: move or resize the source box. The tool switches to Source by itself after you draw an outline.
options.Overgang:: Width in pixels of the soft edge around the outline, where the replacement blends into the surroundings. Larger values hide the transition better but need more room around the object.
options.Toepassen: Replaces the object with the content of the source box (Enter does the same).

d083.tips: Draw the outline a little outside the object, so its shadow and edge are included. Choose a source with the same structure as the place of the object, for example the same floor or wall; the colors are adjusted automatically. Large objects are best removed in a few smaller steps.

d136.about: The Marker paints like a felt-tip marker: translucent ink with a fairly hard edge.
d136.use: Drag with the left mouse button to draw with the foreground color, or with the right mouse button for the background color. Within one stroke the ink does not build up, even if you go back and forth. Where a new stroke crosses an earlier one, the colors multiply and get darker, just like real marker ink. On white the ink keeps its own color; on dark areas it hardly shows.

options.Grootte:: Width of the marker tip in pixels.
options.Dekking:: How strong the ink is. Lower values give a lighter, more transparent line.

d136.tips: Use the Marker for highlighting parts of an image or for drawing on a light background. Work on a separate layer if you want to be able to adjust or remove the lines later.

d137.about: The Palette Knife applies thick, opaque paint with a flat blade, like a painter's palette knife. The blade lies across the direction of the stroke and leaves fine ridges in the paint.
d137.use: Drag with the left mouse button to apply the foreground color, or with the right mouse button for the background color. The knife picks up some of the paint that is already there and drags it along, so colors mix where you work over existing paint. The paint slowly runs out during a long stroke.

options.Grootte:: Width of the blade in pixels.
options.Dekking:: How opaque the paint is.
options.Lading:: How much paint is on the knife. At high values the paint lasts the whole stroke; at low values it runs out sooner and the underlying colors take over.
options.Viscositeit:: How much of the underlying paint the knife picks up and smears along. Higher values mix more.

d137.tips: Short strokes in different directions give a lively, textured surface. Combine it with the Oil Brush for a painted look.

82b3.about: Darkens the bright areas of a photo while leaving the shadows alone, using a soft local brightness mask. Use it when a bright sky or background is washed out compared with your subject.

params.Sterkte: How much the highlights are darkened; higher values pull bright areas down further, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

818e.about: Corrects the strong bulging of a fisheye lens by remapping the image around its centre so that straight lines curve less. The corners stay in place while the centre is compressed.

params.Sterkte: How strongly the fisheye bulge is flattened; higher values give a stronger correction, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

8240.about: Automatically improves a photo in one click: it stretches the tonal range per channel to remove a colour cast, corrects overall brightness towards a balanced middle and adds a little saturation. Useful as a quick first fix for dull or tinted snapshots.

82f1.about: Removes digital camera noise in one click with medium settings. Brightness grain is smoothed with an edge preserving filter and colour blotches are smoothed more strongly, while edges stay sharp.

82d9.about: Finds purple and blue-violet fringes that appear next to high contrast edges and turns them into neutral grey. Use it on photos with purple halos around branches, window frames or other bright edges.

82c1.about: Reduces the grain and colour noise of digital camera photos with an edge preserving filter. Brightness noise and colour noise are treated separately, and you can optionally sharpen the result afterwards.

params.Correctie (sterkte): How strongly noise is smoothed; higher values remove more grain and colour blotches but can make surfaces look plastic, 0 skips the noise removal.
params.Details behouden %: How much of the original fine brightness detail is mixed back in; higher values keep more texture (and some grain), lower values give a smoother result.
params.Verscherpen: Amount of sharpening applied after the noise removal; 0 means no sharpening, higher values make edges crisper.

8307.about: Smooths skin while keeping other areas sharp. It detects skin coloured pixels automatically and applies an edge preserving blur only there, which softens blemishes and pores in portraits.

params.Mate: How strongly skin areas are smoothed; 0 leaves the image unchanged, 100 applies the full smoothing to detected skin.

82b1.about: Brightens the dark areas of a photo while leaving the highlights mostly untouched, like a flash fill light. Use it for subjects that are too dark against a bright background, such as backlit portraits.

params.Sterkte: How much the shadows are lightened; higher values brighten dark areas more, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

82c4.about: Reduces coloured fringes (chromatic aberration) along edges. Near edges, colours that differ strongly from their surroundings are pulled towards the surrounding colour while the brightness stays the same.

params.Straal: How far from an edge fringes are searched and how wide the comparison area is; use larger values for wider fringes.
params.Sterkte: How strongly the fringe colours are neutralised; higher values remove more colour, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

82dc.about: Shifts the colour balance separately in the shadows, midtones or highlights. Use it to remove a colour cast or to warm up or cool down a specific tonal range.

params.Bereik: Which tonal range is adjusted: Shadows affects dark pixels, Midtones affects middle grey values most, Highlights affects bright pixels.
params.Cyaan - rood: Negative values add cyan, positive values add red to the chosen range.
params.Magenta - groen: Negative values add magenta, positive values add green to the chosen range.
params.Geel - blauw: Negative values add yellow, positive values add blue to the chosen range.
params.Helderheid behouden: When on, the brightness of every pixel is restored after the colour shift, so only the colour changes and the image does not get lighter or darker.

806e.about: Automatically finds red eyes (red pupils from a camera flash) and removes the red there, also darkening them slightly. Only small, isolated red spots of eye size are corrected; large red areas such as clothing, a ball or a wall are left alone. With a selection, only the selected area is searched.

params.Sterkte: How much of the correction is applied to the detected red-eye pixels; higher values remove more red, 0 does nothing.
params.Max. oogdiameter (%): The largest size an eye may have in the photo, as a percentage of the longest side of the image. Raise it for close-up portraits where the eyes are large; lower it when red objects slightly larger than an eye are affected.

82d8.about: A photo fix with manual control. It can start with the same automatic colour balance and levels as One Step Photo Fix and then lets you fine tune brightness, shadows, highlights, saturation and sharpness.

params.Helderheid algemeen: Changes overall brightness with a gamma curve; positive values brighten the midtones, negative values darken them.
params.Schaduwen: Positive values lighten the dark areas, negative values darken them.
params.Lichte delen: Positive values lighten the bright areas, negative values darken them to recover detail.
params.Verzadiging: Positive values make colours more vivid, negative values make them duller up to grey at -100.
params.Focus (verscherpen): Amount of sharpening applied at the end; 0 means no sharpening, higher values give crisper detail.
params.Automatisch kleurbalans/niveaus: When on, the image is first auto corrected (tonal range stretched, colour cast removed, brightness balanced) before your other settings are applied.

818c.about: Corrects pincushion distortion, where straight lines bow inward towards the centre (common with telephoto lenses). The image is remapped around its centre while the corners stay in place.

params.Sterkte: How strongly the distortion is corrected; higher values push the centre outward more, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

818d.about: Corrects barrel distortion, where straight lines bulge outward away from the centre (common with wide angle lenses). The image is remapped around its centre while the corners stay in place.

params.Sterkte: How strongly the bulge is corrected; higher values compress the centre more, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

82fb.about: Simulates a shallow depth of field: an elliptical area in the centre stays sharp and the surroundings are blurred, with a smooth transition. Useful to draw attention to a subject in the middle of the image.

params.Focusgrootte %: Size of the sharp ellipse in the centre as a percentage of the image size; larger values keep more of the image sharp.
params.Vervaging: How strongly the area outside the focus is blurred; 0 leaves the image unchanged.
params.Doezelen %: Width of the transition between the sharp and the blurred area; higher values give a softer, more gradual fade.

806f.about: Automatically removes thin vertical scratches, such as those on scanned film or old photos. Pixels that differ strongly from their horizontal neighbours along a vertical line are replaced with a median of those neighbours.

params.Lichte krassen verwijderen: When on, scratches that are lighter than their surroundings are removed.
params.Donkere krassen verwijderen: When on, scratches that are darker than their surroundings are removed.
params.Sterkte: Mild only removes clear, narrow scratches; Normal and Strong detect fainter and wider scratches but may also soften real vertical detail.

806d.about: Removes the comb-like stripes in frames captured from interlaced video. It keeps every other scan line and replaces the lines in between with the average of the lines above and below.

params.Behouden scanlijnen: Which set of lines is kept: Odd or Even. The other set is rebuilt; try the other option if the result still looks jagged.

8089.about: Adds random noise to the image, for a film grain look or to hide banding and over smooth areas.

params.Ruis %: How strong the noise is; higher values give a coarser, more visible grain, 0 adds nothing.
params.Type: Random adds normally distributed grain: mostly small variations with an occasional strong speck, like real film grain. Uniform spreads all variations evenly with no strong specks, which looks flatter and more even. Both have the same overall strength.
params.Kleur: Color adds separate noise to each colour channel (coloured specks); Monochrome adds the same noise to all channels, so the grain is grey.

8066.about: Replaces each pixel with the median colour of the pixels around it. This removes isolated specks and dust while keeping edges sharper than a normal blur.

params.Straal: Size of the area around each pixel that is examined; higher values remove larger specks but also more fine detail.

8074.about: Removes isolated light and dark specks (salt and pepper noise, dust) by replacing only the pixels that differ strongly from the median of their neighbourhood. The rest of the image stays untouched.

params.Vlekgrootte: Largest speck size that should be removed; higher values handle bigger spots but examine a wider area.
params.Gevoeligheid: How easily a pixel is treated as a speck; higher values also correct pixels that differ only a little from their surroundings.

806b.about: Reduces the blocky patterns and ringing that heavy JPEG compression leaves behind, using an edge preserving smoothing filter.

params.Sterkte: How much smoothing is applied, from Low to Maximum; stronger settings remove more artefacts but also more fine detail.
params.Scherpte: Brings back some original detail and adds light sharpening after the cleanup; 0 gives the smoothest result.

806c.about: Reduces moiré patterns, the wavy interference patterns that appear when scanning printed material or photographing fine textures. It blurs fine brightness detail lightly and colour detail more strongly.

params.Fijne details: Strength of the blur on fine patterns; higher values remove coarser moiré but make the image softer, 0 skips this step.
params.Kleurbanden verwijderen: Extra blur on the colour information only, to remove coloured bands without affecting brightness detail; 0 skips this step.

808a.about: Removes small specks and dust by replacing every pixel with the median of its 3 by 3 neighbourhood. A quick cleanup without settings.

8068.about: Smooths flat areas and noise while keeping edges crisp, using an edge preserving filter. Useful to clean up skin, skies or noisy surfaces without blurring outlines.

params.Mate: How strongly the image is smoothed; higher values use a larger area and smooth over bigger differences, and above 50 the filter is applied twice. 0 leaves the image unchanged.

8067.about: Smooths only the flat, low detail areas of the image and leaves textured areas alone. Use it to remove noise from smooth regions without losing texture such as hair or fabric.

params.Mate: How strongly flat areas are smoothed and how much local variation still counts as flat; higher values smooth more, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

8075.about: Remaps the tones of the image with a curve you draw. Points above the diagonal brighten those tones and points below darken them; an S shape adds contrast.

params.Curve: The tone curve: the horizontal axis is the original value and the vertical axis is the new value. Drag points to reshape it; the curve is drawn smoothly through your points.
params.Kanaal: RGB applies the curve to all three channels together; Red, Green or Blue applies it to that channel only, which shifts the colour.

8063.about: Turns the image into pure black and white: every pixel brighter than the threshold becomes white, everything else becomes black. Useful for line art, scanned text or graphic effects.

params.Drempel: Brightness level that separates black from white; higher values make more of the image black, lower values make more of it white.

8052.about: Adjusts overall brightness and contrast of the image.

params.Helderheid: Value added to every channel; positive values lighten the image, negative values darken it.
params.Contrast: Positive values spread the tones away from middle grey for more contrast, negative values pull them towards grey for a flatter look.

8070.about: Remaps the tonal range with input limits, a gamma value and output limits. Use it to fix exposure precisely or to compress the range of an image.

params.Invoer laag: Input value that becomes the output minimum; everything darker is clipped to it. Raising it deepens the shadows.
params.Invoer hoog: Input value that becomes the output maximum; everything brighter is clipped to it. Lowering it brightens the highlights.
params.Gamma × 100: Midtone curve times 100; values above 100 brighten the midtones, values below 100 darken them.
params.Uitvoer min: Darkest value in the result; raising it makes the blacks lighter and lowers contrast.
params.Uitvoer max: Brightest value in the result; lowering it makes the whites darker and lowers contrast.

8056.about: Redistributes the brightness values so that all levels are used about equally, based on the image histogram. This often strongly increases contrast in flat images; colours are shifted by the same brightness change.

8057.about: Automatically stretches each colour channel so its darkest and brightest values (ignoring the extreme 0.5 percent) span the full range. This improves contrast in dull images and can also remove a colour cast.

8053.about: Adjusts the shadows, midtones and highlights separately through a smooth tone curve applied to brightness. Use it to open up dark areas or tame bright areas without changing the colours.

params.Schaduw: Positive values lighten the dark tones, negative values darken them.
params.Middentoon: Positive values lighten the middle tones, negative values darken them.
params.Lichte delen: Positive values lighten the bright tones, negative values darken them.

8060.about: Sets the black point, white point and midtone gamma of the image. A classic way to correct exposure and contrast.

params.Invoer zwart: Input value that becomes pure black; raising it makes the shadows darker and increases contrast.
params.Invoer wit: Input value that becomes pure white; lowering it makes the highlights brighter and increases contrast.
params.Gamma × 100: Midtone curve times 100; values above 100 brighten the midtones, values below 100 darken them.

806a.about: Increases local contrast (clarity) by boosting the difference between each pixel and its smoothed surroundings, mostly in the midtones. This makes hazy or flat photos look crisper and more defined.

params.Sterkte: How strongly local contrast is boosted; higher values give a punchier, more detailed look.

8062.about: Builds one colour channel from a mix of the red, green and blue channels. Useful for creative colour changes and for custom black and white conversions.

params.Uitvoerkanaal: The channel (Red, Green or Blue) that is replaced by the mix; the other channels stay as they are.
params.Rood %: How much of the original red channel goes into the mix; negative values subtract it.
params.Groen %: How much of the original green channel goes into the mix; negative values subtract it.
params.Blauw %: How much of the original blue channel goes into the mix; negative values subtract it.
params.Constante %: A fixed amount added to the mix; positive values brighten the output channel, negative values darken it.
params.Monochroom: When on, the mix is written to all three channels, giving a greyscale image based on your percentages.

8054.about: Adjusts the red, green and blue channels individually. Use it to correct a colour cast or to tint the image.

params.Rood %: Positive values push the red channel towards full, negative values scale it down towards zero.
params.Groen %: Positive values push the green channel towards full, negative values scale it down towards zero.
params.Blauw %: Positive values push the blue channel towards full, negative values scale it down towards zero.

8064.about: Restores faded photos by stretching the tonal range of each channel and boosting saturation. Useful for old prints or scans that have become pale and washed out.

params.Mate: How strongly the image is corrected; higher values clip more of the extremes, add more saturation and apply the correction more fully, 0 leaves the image unchanged.

804a.about: Gives the whole image a single colour while keeping its brightness, like a tinted monochrome photo. Useful for sepia or other toned looks.

params.Kleurtoon: The colour of the tint, on a 0 to 255 scale around the colour wheel (0 is red, around 85 green, around 170 blue).
params.Verzadiging: How intense the tint is; 0 gives grey, 255 gives the strongest colour.

8076.about: Shifts the hue, saturation and lightness of all colours in the image.

params.Kleurtoon: Rotates every colour around the colour wheel by this number of degrees.
params.Verzadiging: Positive values make colours more vivid, negative values make them duller up to grey at -100.
params.Helderheid: Positive values lighten the image towards white, negative values darken it towards black.

805f.about: Changes one specific hue into another and adjusts its saturation, leaving other colours alone. For example, you can turn a red car blue or make only the greens more vivid.

params.Bronkleurtoon: The hue (0 to 359 degrees) you want to change.
params.Bereik: How many degrees around the source hue are affected; larger values include more neighbouring colours, with a soft falloff.
params.Doelkleurtoon: The hue (0 to 359 degrees) the selected colours are shifted to.
params.Verzadiging: Positive values make the affected colours more vivid, negative values make them duller.

82db.about: Sharpens by blending a high pass version of the image (the fine detail only) back onto itself with a contrast blend mode. Gives strong, controllable sharpening of edges and texture.

params.Straal: Size of the detail that is enhanced; small values sharpen fine detail, large values boost broader local contrast.
params.Sterkte: How much of the sharpening blend is applied; 0 leaves the image unchanged, 100 applies it fully.
params.Mengmodus: How the detail is blended: Overlay and Hard Light give strong contrast, Soft Light gives a gentler result.

8086.about: Applies a stronger fixed sharpening than Sharpen, increasing the contrast of small details and edges. No settings.

809b.about: Sharpens the image by increasing contrast where it differs from a blurred copy, with control over size, amount and a threshold. The most flexible way to sharpen photos.

params.Straal: Size of the blur used for comparison; small values sharpen fine detail, larger values give broader, more pronounced edges.
params.Sterkte: How much the detected differences are amplified, in percent; higher values give stronger sharpening.
params.Clip: Minimum difference a pixel must have before it is sharpened; higher values leave smooth areas and noise alone and only sharpen clear edges.

8085.about: Applies a light fixed sharpening that increases the contrast of small details and edges. No settings.

808f.about: Blurs the image along a straight line in one direction, as if the camera or subject moved during the exposure. Useful to suggest speed.

params.Hoek: Direction of the motion in degrees; 0 is horizontal and 90 is vertical.
params.Sterkte (px): Length of the motion trail in pixels; higher values give a longer, stronger blur.

80b5.about: Softens the whole image with a smooth blur, with correct handling of transparent areas. Useful for backgrounds, reducing detail or creating soft effects.

params.Straal: Size of the blur in pixels; higher values make the image softer.

8065.about: Replaces every pixel by the plain average of a square block around it (with correct handling of transparent areas). Compared with Gaussian Blur the result looks harder and slightly blocky at large radius, which can be useful for a deliberate smeared or diffuse effect.

params.Straal: Half the width of the square block that is averaged; higher values give a stronger, more blocky blur.

8084.about: A stronger version of Blur: it averages over a larger area and then once more over the direct neighbours. Use it when Blur is not enough to smooth noise or detail.

8288.about: Blurs the image around a center point, either by rotating, zooming or twisting it, which suggests spinning or fast forward motion.

params.Type: The kind of blur: Draaien smears pixels along circles around the center, Zoomen smears them outward along lines from the center, and Kronkelen combines a small rotation and zoom along a spiral.
params.Sterkte: How long the blur streaks are; 0 leaves the image unchanged and higher values give a stronger blur.
params.Horizontale verschuiving %: Moves the center of the blur left (negative) or right (positive) from the middle of the image, as a percentage of half the width.
params.Verticale verschuiving %: Moves the center of the blur up (negative) or down (positive) from the middle of the image, as a percentage of half the height.
params.Kronkelgraden: Only used with Kronkelen: how much extra twist is added, strongest near the center and fading toward the edge; negative values twist the other way.

8083.about: Blurs the image by giving every pixel the plain average of itself and its eight neighbours. This clearly softens noise and jagged edges, and fine detail fades noticeably.

8088.about: A stronger version of Soften with a larger, smoothly weighted area. It gives a softer look than Soften while keeping more detail than Blur More; useful for portraits or noisy areas.

8087.about: Softens the image gently: the pixel itself counts much more than its neighbours, so harsh edges become smoother while fine detail stays more visible than with Blur. Good for taking the edge off without losing sharpness overall.

8192.about: Gives a dreamy, soft focus look by mixing a blurred copy over the image and optionally adding a glowing halo around bright areas.

params.Zachtheid: How much of the blurred copy is mixed in; 0 keeps the image sharp and 100 makes it very soft.
params.Halo hoeveelheid: How strongly bright areas glow; higher values also lower the brightness at which the glow starts, so more of the image gets a halo. 0 turns the halo off.
params.Halo grootte: How far the glow spreads around bright areas; higher values give a wider, softer halo.

8079.about: Converts the image to shades of gray using the standard luminance weights for red, green and blue. Transparency is kept.

804b.about: Inverts every color so you get a negative, as with photographic film. Transparency is not changed; applying it twice restores the original.

807c.about: Lets you build your own convolution filter: each pixel becomes a weighted sum of itself and its neighbors in a 5x5 grid. Use it to make custom blur, sharpen, emboss or edge filters.

params.Rij 1 kol 1: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows above and 2 columns to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 1 kol 2: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows above and 1 column to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 1 kol 3: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows above of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 1 kol 4: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows above and 1 column to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 1 kol 5: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows above and 2 columns to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 2 kol 1: The weight of the neighbor 1 row above and 2 columns to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 2 kol 2: The weight of the neighbor 1 row above and 1 column to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 2 kol 3: The weight of the neighbor 1 row above of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 2 kol 4: The weight of the neighbor 1 row above and 1 column to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 2 kol 5: The weight of the neighbor 1 row above and 2 columns to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 3 kol 1: The weight of the neighbor 2 columns to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 3 kol 2: The weight of the neighbor 1 column to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 3 kol 3: The weight of the pixel itself (the center of the 5x5 grid); the default 1 with all other cells at 0 leaves the image unchanged.
params.Rij 3 kol 4: The weight of the neighbor 1 column to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 3 kol 5: The weight of the neighbor 2 columns to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 4 kol 1: The weight of the neighbor 1 row below and 2 columns to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 4 kol 2: The weight of the neighbor 1 row below and 1 column to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 4 kol 3: The weight of the neighbor 1 row below of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 4 kol 4: The weight of the neighbor 1 row below and 1 column to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 4 kol 5: The weight of the neighbor 1 row below and 2 columns to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 5 kol 1: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows below and 2 columns to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 5 kol 2: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows below and 1 column to the left of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 5 kol 3: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows below of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 5 kol 4: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows below and 1 column to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Rij 5 kol 5: The weight of the neighbor 2 rows below and 2 columns to the right of the pixel; positive values add that neighbor's color, negative values subtract it.
params.Deler: The weighted sum is divided by this number; set it to the sum of the weights to keep the overall brightness the same.
params.Basis: A value added to every result after dividing; positive values brighten and negative values darken the image.
params.Absolute waarde (anders afkappen): When on, negative results become positive (useful for edge detection filters); when off, negative results are clipped to black.
params.Ook alfakanaal filteren: When on, the transparency channel is filtered with the same matrix as the colors; when off, transparency is left unchanged.

80b2.about: Lights the inside edge of the image or of the opaque area (such as a selection on a transparent layer) as if it were a raised, beveled shape. Useful for buttons and text.

params.Afschuining: The profile of the bevel: Schuin is a straight slope, Rond a rounded convex edge, Hol a concave edge, Dubbel two stacked rounded steps, Rug a ridge that rises and falls again, and Getrapt three flat steps like a staircase.
params.Breedte: How far the bevel reaches into the image or selection from its edge, in pixels; higher values give a wider bevel.
params.Gladheid: Blurs the bevel profile so the slope becomes softer; higher values round off hard ridges and steps.
params.Diepte: The height of the bevel; higher values give stronger light and shadow, so the edge looks deeper.
params.Omgevingslicht: Brightens (positive) or darkens (negative) the whole result before the light is applied.
params.Glans: Adds a shiny highlight; higher values give a stronger, tighter specular spot on the slope that faces the light.
params.Hoek: The direction the light comes from in degrees, where 0 is the top and values increase clockwise (315 is the top left).
params.Intensiteit: How strongly the light and shadow are applied to the slope; 0 shows almost no shading.
params.Hoogte: The elevation of the light above the image; low values give long, strong shading, 90 lights the bevel from straight above.
params.Kleur: The color of the light that falls on the bevel and its highlights.

80b3.about: Adds a lit, beveled rim outside the edge of the opaque area of a layer, so the object looks like it sits on a raised frame. On an image without transparency the bevel is placed on the inside of the image border instead.

params.Afschuining: The profile of the bevel: Schuin is a straight slope, Rond a rounded convex edge, Hol a concave edge, Dubbel two stacked rounded steps, Rug a ridge that rises and falls again, and Getrapt three flat steps like a staircase.
params.Breedte: How far the bevel reaches outward from the edge of the opaque area, in pixels; higher values give a wider bevel.
params.Gladheid: Blurs the bevel profile so the slope becomes softer; higher values round off hard ridges and steps.
params.Diepte: The height of the bevel; higher values give stronger light and shadow, so the edge looks deeper.
params.Omgevingslicht: Brightens (positive) or darkens (negative) the whole result before the light is applied.
params.Glans: Adds a shiny highlight; higher values give a stronger, tighter specular spot on the slope that faces the light.
params.Hoek: The direction the light comes from in degrees, where 0 is the top and values increase clockwise (315 is the top left).
params.Intensiteit: How strongly the light and shadow are applied to the slope; 0 shows almost no shading.
params.Hoogte: The elevation of the light above the image; low values give long, strong shading, 90 lights the bevel from straight above.
params.Kleur: The color of the light that falls on the bevel and its highlights.

80a0.about: Turns the image into a button by lightening the top and left edges and darkening the bottom and right edges, so it looks raised.

params.Hoogte: The thickness in pixels of the top and bottom edges of the button.
params.Breedte: The thickness in pixels of the left and right edges of the button.
params.Dekking: How strongly the edges are lightened and darkened; higher values give more contrast.
params.Rand: Transparant shades the image's own pixels so they show through the edge with a soft fade inward; Massief paints the edges with shades of the chosen color instead.
params.Kleur: The base color of the edges when Rand is set to Massief; it is ignored for Transparant.

80a2.about: Adds a chiseled, lit border. On a layer with transparency the border is added around the outside of the opaque shape; on an image without transparency it is carved into the edge of the image.

params.Grootte: The width of the chiseled border in pixels.
params.Transparant: When on, the border uses the image itself (or plain light and shadow around a shape); when off, the border is filled with the chosen color and then lit.
params.Kleur: The color of the border when Transparant is off.

809f.about: Makes the image look as if a hole was cut into it, by casting a shadow from the transparent surroundings onto the inside of the shape. Use it on a selection or on a layer with transparency.

params.Verticaal: Shifts the shadow down (positive) or up (negative), in pixels.
params.Horizontaal: Shifts the shadow right (positive) or left (negative), in pixels.
params.Dekking: How dark and solid the shadow is.
params.Vervaging: How soft the shadow edge is; 0 gives a hard edge.
params.Binnenkant opvullen met kleur: When on, the inside of the hole is filled with the fill color instead of showing the original image.
params.Opvulkleur: The color used for the inside of the hole when filling is turned on.

809e.about: Adds a shadow behind the opaque parts of a layer, offset and softened, so the object seems to float above the background. The shadow only shows where the layer is transparent.

params.Verticaal: Shifts the shadow down (positive) or up (negative), in pixels.
params.Horizontaal: Shifts the shadow right (positive) or left (negative), in pixels.
params.Dekking: How dark and solid the shadow is.
params.Vervaging: How soft the shadow is; 0 gives a hard edged shadow.
params.Kleur: The color of the shadow.

8188.about: Makes the image tile without visible seams, so you can use it as a repeating background or pattern.

params.Methode: Rand blends the image with a copy shifted by half its size near the edges, Hoek does the same but uses the nearest edge so the blend is concentrated in the corners, and Spiegelen mirrors the image so the edges always match.
params.Richting: Whether the tile must match left to right (Horizontaal), top to bottom (Verticaal) or both (Bidirectioneel).
params.Overgang (%): How wide the blended zone near the edges is; higher values give a smoother but larger transition. Not used with Spiegelen.

80c2.about: Curls up one corner of the image like a page of paper, showing the back of the paper and a soft shadow on the image.

params.Hoek: Which corner of the image curls up.
params.Breedte (%): How far along the horizontal edge the curl reaches, as a percentage of the image width.
params.Hoogte (%): How far along the vertical edge the curl reaches, as a percentage of the image height.
params.Straal: The size of the roll of the curl; higher values give a fatter, rounder curl.
params.Kleur krul: The color of the back of the paper that is visible on the curl.
params.Randmodus: What fills the area uncovered by the curl: Transparant leaves it transparent, Achtergrondkleur fills it with the background color.

80bb.about: Shifts the whole image horizontally and vertically. With the default wrap mode and 50% offsets the edges move to the middle, which helps you check and fix seams when making tiles.

params.Horizontale verschuiving (%): How far to move the image right (positive) or left (negative), as a percentage of its width.
params.Verticale verschuiving (%): How far to move the image down (positive) or up (negative), as a percentage of its height.
params.Randmodus: What fills the uncovered area: Achtergrondkleur uses the background color, Herhalen stretches the edge pixels, Transparant leaves it transparent and Omloop brings back the part that was pushed off the other side.

804c.about: Reduces the number of brightness levels per color channel, giving flat bands of color like a poster.

params.Niveaus: How many levels each of red, green and blue may have; low values give strong banding, high values look close to the original.

81f1.about: Scatters spheres over the image: transparent soap bubbles or solid shiny balls colored from the image below. Each ball or bubble is lit from the top left.

params.Dekking van canvas: How much of the image is covered; higher values place more balls or bubbles.
params.Gemiddelde grootte: The average diameter of the balls or bubbles in pixels.
params.Grootte-variatie: How much the sizes differ from the average; 0 makes them all the same size.
params.Type: Bellen draws see through bubbles with a bright rim and highlight; Ballen draws opaque balls colored by the pixel at their center.
params.Willekeurig getal: The random seed that determines the positions and sizes; change it to get a different arrangement.

80ab.about: Gives the image a polished metal look by turning its brightness into repeating light and dark bands with bright highlights.

params.Vouwen: How many light and dark bands the brightness range is folded into; higher values give a busier, more reflective look.
params.Helderheid: Shifts the bands lighter (above 50) or darker (below 50).
params.Oorspronkelijke kleur gebruiken: When on, the original colors of the image are kept in the metal; when off, the chosen color is used.
params.Kleur: The metal color used when the original colors are not used.

80c9.about: Draws contour lines, like on a map, along places where the brightness of the image crosses fixed steps.

params.Afstand: The brightness step between lines; low values give many close lines, high values only a few.
params.Lijnkleur: The color of the contour lines.

80bf.about: Makes the image look like it is covered in shiny enamel, with raised, lit color areas based on the brightness of the image.

params.Detail: How sharp the steps between enamel areas are and how high they stand; higher values give crisper, deeper relief.
params.Dichtheid: How many brightness steps become separate enamel areas; higher values give more, smaller areas.
params.Dikte: How thick and smooth the enamel layer is; higher values blur more detail away.
params.Hoek: The direction the light comes from in degrees, where 0 is the top and values increase clockwise.
params.Kleur: The color of the light and the shine on the enamel.

80cc.about: Covers the image with a shiny, rainbow colored foil whose colors follow the brightness of the image, mixed with the original.

params.Vervaging: Blurs the image before the foil is made, giving smoother color bands and relief.
params.Detail: How strong the embossed relief and highlights on the foil are.
params.Dichtheid: How quickly the colors change with brightness; higher values give more color bands.

80c7.about: Finds the edges in the image and colors them with the chosen color, leaving the rest of the image as it is.

params.Detail: Higher values detect finer edges; lower values only pick up broad, soft edges.
params.Intensiteit: How many edges are colored and how strongly; higher values give thicker, more visible edges.
params.Kleur: The color painted on the edges.

80a1.about: Makes the image look as if it was dipped in hot wax: it is softened, tinted with the foreground color and given a glossy, lit relief.

818b.about: Recreates the image as a print raster of dots, lines or squares, like in newspapers and comics.

params.Halftoonpatroon: The shape of the raster: Rond uses dots, Lijn uses parallel lines and Vierkant uses squares.
params.Grootte: The size of one raster cell in pixels; larger values give a coarser pattern.
params.Rasterhoek: The angle of the raster in degrees.
params.Kleurenschema: Grijswaarden makes black dots on white based on brightness; RGB makes a separate raster for red, green and blue, each at a slightly different angle, for a colored result.

80a8.about: Turns the edges of the image into glowing neon lines in vivid colors on a dark background. The neon color is the opposite hue of the original color.

params.Intensiteit: How bright the lines are and how far the glow spreads.
params.Scherpte: Higher values detect finer, sharper edges; lower values give broader, softer lines.

80a7.about: Shows only the edges of the image as bright colored lines on black, as if they light up.

params.Intensiteit: How bright the glowing edges are.
params.Scherpte: Higher values keep fine detail and make the lines brighter; lower values blur first so only coarse edges remain.

80c4.about: Makes the image look like a yellowed old newspaper photo: grayscale, lower contrast, a paper tone, stains and some grain.

params.Aantal jaren: How old the paper looks; higher values give more yellow, more blur, more stains and lower contrast.

804d.about: Inverts all color values brighter than the threshold, creating the strange partly negative look of a solarized photo.

params.Drempel: Channel values above this level are inverted; lower values invert more of the image.

80bd.about: Turns the brightness of the image into stacked terraces, like a relief map, and lights them so each level casts a shadow.

params.Breedte: How sloped the terrace edges are; higher values give wider, softer slopes.
params.Dichtheid: How many terrace levels are made; higher values give more, thinner levels.
params.Hoek: The direction the light comes from in degrees, where 0 is the top and values increase clockwise.
params.Kleur: The color of the light on the terraces.

81e5.about: Places a round magnifying lens on the image that enlarges what is under it, with a darker rim and a glass highlight.

params.Midden X %: The horizontal position of the lens center, as a percentage of the image width.
params.Midden Y %: The vertical position of the lens center, as a percentage of the image height.
params.Straal %: The size of the lens relative to the shorter side of the image.
params.Vergroting %: How much the center of the lens enlarges; 100 means no enlargement and 500 is five times.

80c6.about: Darkens the image and lights it with up to two colored spotlights, as if it were lit on a stage.

params.Duisternis: How much the whole image is darkened before the lamps light it; higher values make the unlit areas darker.
params.Lamp 1 kleur: The color of the light of lamp 1.
params.Lamp 1 horizontaal %: The horizontal position of lamp 1, as a percentage of the image width.
params.Lamp 1 verticaal %: The vertical position of lamp 1, as a percentage of the image height.
params.Lamp 1 richting: The direction lamp 1 points in degrees, where 0 is up and values increase clockwise (180 points down).
params.Lamp 1 kegelgrootte: The width of the light cone of lamp 1; higher values give a wider beam.
params.Lamp 2 kleur: The color of the light of lamp 2.
params.Lamp 2 horizontaal %: The horizontal position of lamp 2, as a percentage of the image width.
params.Lamp 2 verticaal %: The vertical position of lamp 2, as a percentage of the image height.
params.Lamp 2 richting: The direction lamp 2 points in degrees, where 0 is up and values increase clockwise (180 points down).
params.Lamp 2 kegelgrootte: The width of the light cone of lamp 2; higher values give a wider beam.

80c5.about: Adds a bright sun with rays, a light spot and a row of lens flare circles toward the center of the image.

params.Kleur: The color of the sunlight, rays and circles.
params.Horizontaal %: The horizontal position of the sun, as a percentage of the image width.
params.Verticaal %: The vertical position of the sun, as a percentage of the image height.
params.Helderheid lichtvlek: How bright the sun spot and its glow are.
params.Dichtheid stralen: How many rays come from the sun; higher values give more, thinner rays.
params.Helderheid stralen: How bright the rays are; 0 hides them.
params.Helderheid cirkels: How bright the lens flare circles between the sun and the center are; 0 hides them.

8319.about: Gives a photo the color character of a type of film and can then place a colored filter over it, like a filter in front of a lens.
